title.zh: 卷14 神元平文諸帝子孫
title.en: Volume 14: Emperor Shenyuan's and Emperor Pingwen's Children and Grandchildren
title.raw: 卷14 神元平文諸帝子孫 Volume 14: Emperor Shenyuan's and Emperor Pingwen's Children and Grandchildren

sentences.zh: 上谷公紇羅，神元皇帝之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Duke of Shanggu Heluo was a great-grandson of Emperor Shenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Heluo, Duke of Shanggu, was a great-grandson of Emperor Shenyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，從太祖自獨孤如賀蘭部，招集舊戶，得三百家，與弟建議，勸賀訥推太祖為主。

translations.literal: At first he followed Taizu from the Dugu clan to the Helan tribe, gathered old households, and obtained three hundred families; with his younger brother Jian he proposed urging Henai to elevate Taizu as chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he followed Taizu from the Dugu to the Helan, rallied three hundred old households, and with his brother Jian urged Henai to make Taizu their leader.

sentences.zh: 及太祖登王位，紇羅常翼衞左右。

translations.literal: When Taizu ascended the royal throne, Heluo constantly guarded close at his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu took the kingship, Heluo served constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 又從征伐，有大功。

translations.literal: He also followed on campaigns and had great merit.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned as well and won great distinction.

sentences.zh: 紇羅有援立謀，特見優賞。

translations.literal: Heluo had merit in the plan to support enthronement and was especially favored and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Because Heluo had helped raise Taizu to power, he received exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 及即帝位，與弟建同日賜爵為公。

translations.literal: When he took the imperial throne, he and his younger brother Jian were enfeoffed as dukes on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu became emperor, he enfeoffed Heluo and Jian as dukes on the same day.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子題，少以雄武知名，賜爵襄城公。

translations.literal: His son Ti was known from youth for martial prowess and was granted the title Duke of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ti won early fame for valor and was made Duke of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 從征中山，受詔徇下諸郡，撫慰新城，皆安化樂業。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Zhongshan he received orders to march through the commanderies below, pacify Xincheng, and all were settled and glad in their work.
translations.idiomatic: On the Zhongshan campaign he was ordered to sweep the lower commanderies; he pacified Xincheng, and the people settled gladly to their trades.

sentences.zh: 進爵為王。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prince.

sentences.zh: 擊慕容驎於義臺，中流矢薨。

translations.literal: He attacked Murong Lin at Yitai, was struck by a flying arrow, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Murong Lin at Yitai, took an arrow in flight, and died.

sentences.zh: 帝以太醫令陰光為視療不盡術，伏法。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Grand Physician Yin Guang's treatment did not exhaust every art, had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that Grand Physician Yin Guang had not done all he could and had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 子悉襲，降爵為襄城公。

translations.literal: His son Xiji succeeded; the title was reduced to Duke of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiji inherited the line but was demoted to Duke of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈襄城王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Prince of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Prince of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 建德公嬰文，神元皇帝之後也。

translations.literal: Duke of Jiande Yingwen was a descendant of Emperor Shenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yingwen, Duke of Jiande, descended from Emperor Shenyuan.

sentences.zh: 少明辯，有決斷，太宗器之。

translations.literal: From youth he was clear in debate and decisive; Emperor Taizong valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and resolute from youth, he won Emperor Taizong's esteem.

sentences.zh: 典出納詔命，常執機要。

translations.literal: He managed outgoing and incoming edicts and orders and often held confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the issuing and receipt of edicts and routinely held the keys of state.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，拜護東夷校尉，進爵建德公，鎮遼西。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, he was appointed Protector of the Eastern Yi, advanced to Duke of Jiande, and stationed at Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizu's accession he became Protector of the Eastern Yi, was raised to Duke of Jiande, and garrisoned Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 真定侯陸，神元皇帝之後也。

translations.literal: Marquis of Zhending Lu was a descendant of Emperor Shenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, Marquis of Zhending, was of Emperor Shenyuan's line.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，以武功頗蒙恩遇，拜散騎常侍，賜爵真定侯。

translations.literal: In Shizu's time, for martial merit he often received favor, was made scattered cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and was granted Marquis of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizu his battlefield service won repeated favor: he became scattered cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and Marquis of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 陸曾孫軌，字法寄，稍遷洛陽令。

translations.literal: Lu's great-grandson Gui, styled Faji, gradually rose to magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu's great-grandson Gui, styled Faji, rose step by step to magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時天下多事，軌惟以深刻遇下，死多酷濫，識者非之。

translations.literal: When the realm had many troubles, Gui treated subordinates only with harsh severity; deaths from cruel excess were many, and the knowing disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: In troubled times Gui ruled his subordinates with pitiless severity; many died from his excesses, and men of judgment condemned him.

sentences.zh: 孝靜時，鄴宮創制，以軌為營構使。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaojing's time, when the Ye palace was first built, Gui was made commissioner of construction.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaojing, when the Ye palace was first laid out, Gui was put in charge of building it.

sentences.zh: 除徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was removed and made Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 軌風望既陋，又無學術，雖歷名位，時人輕之。

translations.literal: Gui's reputation was already mean and he lacked learning; though he held famous posts, men of the time looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's standing was already low and he had no scholarship; for all his grand titles, his contemporaries held him cheap.

sentences.zh: 卒於州。

translations.literal: He died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving in the province.

sentences.zh: 武陵侯因，章帝之後也。

translations.literal: Marquis of Wuling Yin was a descendant of Emperor Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, Marquis of Wuling, came down from Emperor Zhang.

sentences.zh: 從太祖平中原，以功封曲逆侯。

translations.literal: He followed Taizu in pacifying the Central Plain and for merit was enfeoffed Marquis of Quni.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizu in pacifying the Central Plain and was enfeoffed Marquis of Quni for his service.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，改爵武陵。

translations.literal: In Shizu's time the title was changed to Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizu his fief was changed to Wuling.

sentences.zh: 長樂王壽樂，章帝之後也。

translations.literal: Prince of Changle Shoule was a descendant of Emperor Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Shoule, Prince of Changle, was of Emperor Zhang's line.

sentences.zh: 位選部尚書，南安王，改封長樂王。

translations.literal: He held office as Minister of the Selection Bureau, Prince of Nan'an, and was changed in enfeoffment to Prince of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of the Selection Bureau and Prince of Nan'an before his fief was changed to Changle.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，壽樂有援立功，拜太宰、大都督、中外諸軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Shoule had merit in supporting enthronement and was appointed Grand Preceptor, grand commander, commander of all armies within and without, and recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozong's accession Shoule was rewarded for helping put him on the throne with Grand Preceptor, grand commander, command of all armies within and without, and the post of recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 矜功，與尚書令長孫渴侯爭權，並伏法。

translations.literal: He boasted of merit, struggled for power with Masters of Writing Chief Zhangsun Kehou, and both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: He grew proud of his service and wrestled for power with Chief of the Masters of Writing Zhangsun Kehou; both men were executed.

sentences.zh: 望都公頹，昭帝之後也。

translations.literal: Duke of Wangdu Tui was a descendant of Emperor Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Tui, Duke of Wangdu, descended from Emperor Zhao.

sentences.zh: 隨太祖平中原，賜爵望都侯。

translations.literal: He followed Taizu in pacifying the Central Plain and was granted Marquis of Wangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizu in pacifying the Central Plain and received Marquis of Wangdu.

sentences.zh: 世祖以頹美儀容，進止可觀，使迎左昭儀於蠕蠕，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Shizu, because Tui's appearance was handsome and his bearing admirable, had him welcome the Left Esteemed Consort from the Ruru and advanced his title to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu thought Tui handsome and dignified in bearing and sent him to fetch the Left Esteemed Consort from the Ruru; his title was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 曲陽侯素延，桓帝之後也。

translations.literal: Marquis of Quyang Suyan was a descendant of Emperor Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Suyan, Marquis of Quyang, was of Emperor Huan's line.

sentences.zh: 以小統從太祖征討諸部，初定并州，為刺史。

translations.literal: As a petty commander he followed Taizu in campaigns against the tribes; when Bing province was first pacified he was made inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a petty commander under Taizu in tribal campaigns; when Bing was first pacified he became its inspector.

sentences.zh: 太祖之驚於栢肆也，并州守將封竇真為逆，素延斬之。

translations.literal: When Taizu was alarmed at Baixi, Bing province's defending general Feng Douzhen rebelled and Suyan beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was thrown into alarm at Baixi, the Bing garrison commander Feng Douzhen turned rebel and Suyan cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 時太祖意欲撫悅新附，悔參合之誅，而素延殺戮過多，坐免官。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu wished to soothe and please the newly attached and regretted the massacre at Canhe, but Suyan's slaughter was excessive and he was dismissed from office for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then meant to win over the newly submitted and regretted the slaughter at Canhe, yet Suyan had killed far too many and was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 中山平，拜幽州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was pacified, he was appointed Inspector of You province.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongshan fell he was made Inspector of You.

sentences.zh: 豪奢放逸，左遷上谷太守。

translations.literal: Extravagant and dissolute, he was demoted to Administrator of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Luxurious and unrestrained, he was demoted to Administrator of Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 後賜爵曲陽侯。

translations.literal: Later he was granted title Marquis of Quyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was enfeoffed Marquis of Quyang.

sentences.zh: 時太祖留心黃老，欲以純風化俗，雖乘輿服御，皆去彫飾，咸尚質儉，而素延奢侈過度，太祖深銜之。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu attended to Huang-Lao, wishing to purify custom by a simple wind; even carriage robes and trappings shed carving and ornament, all honoring plain frugality, while Suyan's luxury exceeded bounds and Taizu deeply harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then turned to Huang-Lao, hoping to refine the people through plain ways: even imperial carriages and robes lost their ornament, yet Suyan's extravagance went beyond measure, and Taizu nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 積其過，因徵，坐賜死。

translations.literal: Accumulating his offenses, he was summoned and sentenced to death by imperial gift.
translations.idiomatic: When his faults piled high he was summoned and granted death.

sentences.zh: 順陽公郁，桓帝之後也。

translations.literal: Duke of Shunyang Yu was a descendant of Emperor Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Duke of Shunyang, came down from Emperor Huan.

sentences.zh: 少忠正亢直。

translations.literal: From youth he was loyal, upright, and unbending.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was loyal, upright, and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 初以羽林中郎內侍，勤幹有稱。

translations.literal: At first, as palace guard central cadet, he served within the palace; diligent and capable, he had a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as a palace-guard cadet within the inner quarters, where diligence won him a name.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，位殿中尚書。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's time he held office as Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong he became Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從高宗東巡臨海，以勞賜爵順陽公。

translations.literal: He followed Gaozong on an eastern tour to the coast; for labor he was granted Duke of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Gaozong on an eastern tour to the sea and, for his exertions, was made Duke of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，乙渾專權，隔絕內外，百官震恐，計無所出。

translations.literal: When Gaozong died, Yifu Hun monopolized power and cut off inside from outside; the hundred officials were shaken and fearful and could find no plan.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong's death Yifu Hun seized power, sealing court from capital; officials trembled and knew no remedy.

sentences.zh: 郁率殿中衞士數百人從順德門入，欲誅渾。

translations.literal: Yu led several hundred palace guards in through Shunde Gate intending to kill Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu led several hundred palace guards through Shunde Gate to kill Hun.

sentences.zh: 渾懼，逆出問郁曰：「君入何意？

translations.literal: Hun was afraid, came out against him, and asked Yu, "Lord, what is your intent in entering?
translations.idiomatic: Hun, afraid, came out to meet him and asked, "My lord, why have you entered?

sentences.zh: 」郁曰：「不見天子，羣臣憂懼，求見主上。

translations.literal: Yu said, "Not seeing the Son of Heaven, the ministers are anxious and fearful and seek audience with the sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "We have not seen the Son of Heaven; the ministers are anxious and beg audience with their lord."

sentences.zh: 」渾窘怖，謂郁曰：「今大行在殯，天子諒闇，故未接百官，諸君何疑？

translations.literal: Hun was distressed and afraid and said to Yu, "Now the late emperor lies in coffin and the Son of Heaven is in mourning darkness, so he has not yet received the officials—why should you lords doubt?
translations.idiomatic: Hun, cornered and afraid, said, "The late emperor still lies in state and the Son of Heaven keeps mourning seclusion, so he has not yet received you—why this suspicion?

sentences.zh: 」遂奉顯祖臨朝。

translations.literal: He then presented Xianzu to hold court.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought Xianzu out to preside at court.

sentences.zh: 後渾心規為亂，朝臣側目，郁復謀殺渾，為渾所誅。

translations.literal: Later Hun's heart plotted rebellion; court ministers watched sidelong. Yu again plotted to kill Hun and was executed by Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hun turned his mind to treason and the court watched him with sidelong eyes. Yu plotted again to kill him and was slain by Hun.

sentences.zh: 顯祖錄郁忠正，追贈順陽王，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Xianzu recorded Yu's loyalty and rectitude, posthumously made him Prince of Shunyang, and gave posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu honored Yu's loyalty, posthumously raised him to Prince of Shunyang, and styled him Jian.

sentences.zh: 宜都王目辰，桓帝之後也。

translations.literal: Prince of Yidu Muchen was a descendant of Emperor Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Muchen, Prince of Yidu, was of Emperor Huan's line.

sentences.zh: 初以羽林郎從太祖南伐至江。

translations.literal: At first, as palace guard, he followed Taizu on the southern campaign as far as the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed Taizu south as a palace guard, campaigning as far as the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，以勞累遷侍中、尚書左僕射，封南平公。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, for accumulated labor he was promoted attendant-in-ordinary and left vice director of the Masters of Writing and was enfeoffed Duke of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozong's accession his long service won him attendant-in-ordinary, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, and the dukedom of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 乙渾之謀亂也，目辰與兄郁議欲殺渾，事泄被誅，目辰逃隱得免。

translations.literal: When Yifu Hun plotted disorder, Muchen and his elder brother Yu discussed killing Hun; the affair leaked and he was condemned, but Muchen fled in hiding and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Yifu Hun rose in treason, Muchen and his brother Yu planned his death; the plot was exposed and Muchen was sentenced, but he hid and escaped.

sentences.zh: 顯祖傳位，有定策勳。

translations.literal: When Xianzu transmitted the throne he had merit in settling the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzu abdicated in favor of the new emperor he had helped fix the succession.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，遷司徒，封宜都王，除雍州刺史，鎮長安。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he was moved to Minister over the Masses, enfeoffed Prince of Yidu, removed and made Inspector of Yong province, and stationed at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozu's accession he became Minister over the Masses and Prince of Yidu, then left court to serve as Inspector of Yong and garrison Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 目辰性亢直耿介，不為朋黨，朝臣咸憚之。

translations.literal: Muchen's nature was unbending, upright, and aloof; he did not join factions, and court ministers all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Muchen was stiff, upright, and aloof, never joining cliques, and the court feared him.

sentences.zh: 然好財利，在州，政以賄成。

translations.literal: Yet he loved profit; in the province government was accomplished through bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved gain, and in Yong his rule ran on bribes.

sentences.zh: 有罪伏法，爵除。

translations.literal: For a crime he was executed; his title was removed.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed for a crime and his fief was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 穆帝長子六脩，少而兇悖。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu's eldest son Liuxiu was from youth fierce and perverse.
translations.idiomatic: Liuxiu, Emperor Mu's eldest son, was violent and unruly from childhood.

sentences.zh: 穆帝五年，遣六脩為前鋒，與輔相衞雄、范班及姬澹等救劉琨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Emperor Mu he sent Liuxiu as vanguard with the assisting minister Wei Xiong, Fan Ban, and Jitan and others to rescue Liu Kun.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Mu's fifth year he sent Liuxiu ahead with the assisting minister Wei Xiong, Fan Ban, Jitan, and others to relieve Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 帝躬統大兵為後繼。

translations.literal: The emperor personally commanded the great army as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself led the main host as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 劉粲懼，焚燒輜重，突圍遁走。

translations.literal: Liu Can was afraid, burned the baggage trains, broke out, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can, in fear, burned his wagons, broke out, and fled.

sentences.zh: 縱騎追之，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: They loosed cavalry in pursuit and killed and wounded very many.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing cavalry killed and wounded a great multitude.

sentences.zh: 帝因大獵於壽陽山，陳閱皮肉，山為變赤。

translations.literal: The emperor then held a great hunt on Shouyang Mountain, displayed the flesh and hides for review, and the mountain turned red with the change.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then hunted on Shouyang Mountain, laid out flesh and hides for inspection, and the slopes ran red.

sentences.zh: 及晉懷帝為劉聰所執，穆帝遣六脩與桓帝子普根率精騎助劉琨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai of Jin was seized by Liu Cong, Emperor Mu sent Liuxiu and Emperor Huan's son Pugen with picked cavalry to aid Liu Kun.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's Emperor Huai fell into Liu Cong's hands, Emperor Mu sent Liuxiu and Emperor Huan's son Pugen with elite horsemen to help Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 初穆帝少子比延有寵，欲以為後。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Mu's youngest son Biyan was favored and he wished to make him successor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu had long favored his youngest son Biyan and meant to make him heir.

sentences.zh: 六脩出居新平城，而黜其母。

translations.literal: Liuxiu was sent out to dwell at Xincheng and his mother was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Liuxiu was sent to live at Xincheng and his mother was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 六脩有驊騮駿馬，日行五百里，穆帝欲取以給比延。

translations.literal: Liuxiu had a bay dappled swift horse that went five hundred li a day; Emperor Mu wished to take it to give to Biyan.
translations.idiomatic: Liuxiu owned a dappled bay that could run five hundred li in a day; Emperor Mu wanted it for Biyan.

sentences.zh: 後六脩來朝，穆帝又命拜比延，六脩不從。

translations.literal: Later when Liuxiu came to court, Emperor Mu again ordered him to bow to Biyan; Liuxiu would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: When Liuxiu later came to court, Emperor Mu again ordered him to bow to Biyan, and Liuxiu refused.

sentences.zh: 穆帝乃坐比延於己所乘步輦，使人導從出遊。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu then seated Biyan on the walking palanquin he himself rode and had men guide and attend him on an outing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu set Biyan on his own walking palanquin and sent attendants to escort him on parade.

sentences.zh: 六脩望見，以為穆帝，謁伏路左，及至，乃是比延，慚怒而去。

translations.literal: Liuxiu saw from afar and thought it was Emperor Mu; he bowed prostrate on the left of the road, but when he came near it was Biyan, and he left in shame and anger.
translations.idiomatic: Liuxiu saw the procession from afar and, thinking it the emperor, bowed by the roadside—only to find Biyan and stalk away in shame and rage.

sentences.zh: 召之，不還。

translations.literal: Summoned, he did not return.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned he would not come back.

sentences.zh: 穆帝怒，率眾伐之。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu was angry and led the multitude to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Emperor Mu marched against him in force.

sentences.zh: 帝軍不利，六脩殺比延。

translations.literal: The emperor's army was unfavorable; Liuxiu killed Biyan.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army fared badly, and Liuxiu killed Biyan.

sentences.zh: 帝改服微行民間，有賤婦人識帝，遂暴崩。

translations.literal: The emperor changed clothes and went incognito among the people; a low woman recognized the emperor and he suddenly died violently.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor disguised himself among commoners; a humble woman recognized him, and he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 普根先守于外，聞難，率眾來赴。

translations.literal: Pugen had first been guarding outside; hearing of the crisis he led troops to come.
translations.idiomatic: Pugen had been holding the field; hearing of the disaster he hurried in with troops.

sentences.zh: 攻六脩，滅之。

translations.literal: He attacked Liuxiu and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Liuxiu down and wiped him out.

sentences.zh: 吉陽男比干，太祖族弟也。

translations.literal: Baron of Jiyang Bigan was Taizu's younger clansman in the same generation.
translations.idiomatic: Bigan, Baron of Jiyang, was Taizu's younger clansman.

sentences.zh: 以司衞監討白澗丁零有功，賜爵吉陽男。

translations.literal: As Director of Palace Guards he campaigned against the Dingling of Baijian with merit and was granted Baron of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: As Director of Palace Guards he campaigned against the Baijian Dingling with success and was made Baron of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 後為南道都將，戰沒。

translations.literal: Later, as commander-in-chief of the southern route, he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Later, commanding the southern army, he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 江夏公呂，太祖族弟也。

translations.literal: Duke of Jiangxia Lü was Taizu's younger clansman in the same generation.
translations.idiomatic: Lü, Duke of Jiangxia, was Taizu's younger clansman.

sentences.zh: 從世祖平涼州有功，封江夏公，位外都大官，委以朝政，大見尊重。

translations.literal: He followed Shizu in pacifying Liang province with merit, was enfeoffed Duke of Jiangxia, held office as chief official of the outer court, and was entrusted with court governance, greatly respected.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizu in pacifying Liang, was made Duke of Jiangxia, headed the outer court, and was entrusted with state affairs to great honor.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈江夏王，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Prince of Jiangxia and buried alongside at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Prince of Jiangxia, buried beside the imperial tombs at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 高涼王孤，平文皇帝之第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Gaoliang Gu was the fourth son of Emperor Pingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Gu, Prince of Gaoliang, was Emperor Pingwen's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 多才藝，有志略。

translations.literal: He had many talents and arts and possessed will and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted in many arts, he was a man of resolve and design.

sentences.zh: 烈帝之前元年，國有內難，昭成如襄國。

translations.literal: In the first year before Emperor Lie, the state had internal difficulty and Emperor Zhaocheng went to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the year before Emperor Lie's reign began, civil strife broke out and Emperor Zhaocheng went to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 後烈帝臨崩，顧命，迎昭成立之，社稷可安。

translations.literal: Later, when Emperor Lie was on the point of death, he left a dying charge: welcome Emperor Zhaocheng and establish him and the altars may be secure.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Lie lay dying he charged them: bring Zhaocheng back and enthrone him, and the realm will be secure.

sentences.zh: 及崩，羣臣咸以新有大故，內外未安，昭成在南，來未可果，比至之間，恐生變詐，宜立長君以鎮眾望。

translations.literal: When he died the ministers all thought there had newly been a great misfortune, inside and outside were not yet settled, Zhaocheng was in the south and his coming could not yet be made certain; in the interval before he arrived they feared fraud and change, and it was fit to establish the eldest as lord to calm public expectation.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the ministers judged the realm too unsettled for a distant heir: Zhaocheng was still in the south, and until he came they feared intrigue; they argued that an elder lord should be set up at once to steady men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 次弟屈，剛猛多變，不如孤之寬和柔順，於是大人梁蓋等殺屈，共推孤。

translations.literal: The next younger brother Qu was fierce and changeable, not like Gu's mildness, compliance, and yielding; thereupon the elders Liang Gai and others killed Qu and together urged Gu.
translations.idiomatic: The next brother Qu was brutal and unpredictable, nothing like Gu's mildness; the elders Liang Gai and others killed Qu and pressed Gu to rule.

sentences.zh: 孤曰：「吾兄居長，自應繼位，我安可越次而處大業。

translations.literal: Gu said, "My elder brother by age should succeed; how could I overstep and occupy the great enterprise?
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "My elder brother should reign by right. How could I leap over him to seize the throne?

sentences.zh: 」乃自詣鄴奉迎，請身留為質。

translations.literal: He then went in person to Ye to welcome him, asking to remain himself as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: He went in person to Ye to fetch him, offering to stay behind as hostage.

sentences.zh: 石虎義而從之。

translations.literal: Shi Hu, in righteousness, assented.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his honor, Shi Hu agreed.

sentences.zh: 昭成即位，乃分國半部以與之。

translations.literal: When Zhaocheng took the throne he then divided half the state and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaocheng came to the throne he gave Gu half the realm.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his princely rank.

sentences.zh: 子斤，失職懷怒，構寔君為逆，死於長安。

translations.literal: His son Jin, having lost office, harbored anger, framed the Veritable Lord in rebellion, and died at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin, stripped of office and bitter, framed the Veritable Lord for treason and met his end at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，以孤勳高，追封高涼王，諡曰神武。

translations.literal: In Taizu's time, because Gu's merit was high, he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Gaoliang with posthumous title Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizu's day Gu's service was judged supreme; he was posthumously made Prince of Gaoliang, styled Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 斤子樂真，[2]頻有戰功，後襲祖封。

translations.literal: Jin's son Lezhen, [2] often had battle merit and later inherited his grandfather's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's son Lezhen, [2] won repeated honors in war and later inherited his grandfather's fief.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，改封平陽王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taizong, his title was changed to Prince of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taizong's reign he was made Prince of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子禮，襲本爵高涼王。

translations.literal: His son Li inherited the original title Prince of Gaoliang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li took up the old title, Prince of Gaoliang.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡懿王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Prince Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was styled Prince Yi.

sentences.zh: 子那，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Na inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Na inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 拜中都大官。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief official of the central court.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief officer of the central court.

sentences.zh: 驍猛善攻戰。

translations.literal: Fierce and valiant, he was skilled in attack and battle.
translations.idiomatic: Bold in assault, he excelled in battle.

sentences.zh: 正平初，坐事伏法。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengping, for an offense he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengping he was executed for a crime.

sentences.zh: 顯祖即位，追那功，命子紇紹封。

translations.literal: When Xianzu took the throne he recalled Na's merit and ordered his son He to continue the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianzu's accession he honored Na's service and had his son He continue the line.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子大曹，性愿直。

translations.literal: His son Dacao was by nature honest and straight.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dacao was plain and upright by nature.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，諸王非太祖子孫者，例降爵為公。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's time, for princes who were not Taizu's descendants titles were as a rule reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu, princes outside Taizu's direct line were routinely demoted from prince to duke.

sentences.zh: 以大曹先世讓國功重，曾祖樂真勳著前朝，改封太原郡公。

translations.literal: Because Dacao's forebears' merit in yielding the state was heavy and great-grandfather Lezhen's merit was illustrious in the former court, he was changed to Duke of Taiyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dacao's house had twice earned the throne's debt—Gu's abdication and Lezhen's battlefield fame—so he was made Duke of Taiyuan commandery instead.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子，國除。

translations.literal: He died without a son; the state was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He died childless and the fief lapsed.

sentences.zh: 世宗又以大曹從兄子洪威紹。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong also had Dacao's elder cousin's son Hongwei continue the line.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong later had Dacao's cousin's son Hongwei carry on the line.

sentences.zh: 恭謙好學，為潁川太守，有政績。

translations.literal: Respectful, modest, and loving learning, as Administrator of Yingchuan he had governing achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Humble, eager to learn, he governed Yingchuan with a record of real achievement.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，在潁川聚眾應關西，齊獻武王遣將討平之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing, at Yingchuan he gathered followers responding to Guanxi; Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu sent generals to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaojing he raised men at Yingchuan in answer to the Guanxi rising; the Prince of Qi, Duke Xianwu, sent generals who crushed him.

sentences.zh: 禮弟陵，世祖賜爵襄邑男。

translations.literal: Li's younger brother Ling—Shizu granted him Baron of Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li's younger brother Ling received Baron of Xiangyi from Shizu.

sentences.zh: 進爵為子。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to viscount.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to viscount.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子瓌，位柔玄鎮司馬。

translations.literal: His son Gui held office as major of Rouxuan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui served as major at Rouxuan garrison.

sentences.zh: 瓌子鷙，字孔雀。

translations.literal: Gui's son Zhi, styled Kongque.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's son Zhi, whose style was Kongque, "Peacock."

sentences.zh: 容貌魁壯，腰帶十圍。

translations.literal: His appearance was tall and strong; his belt was ten arm-spans.
translations.idiomatic: He was huge in frame, his belt ten arm-spans round.

sentences.zh: 為羽林隊仗副。

translations.literal: He was deputy of the Feathered Forest guard detachment.
translations.idiomatic: He served as deputy commander of a Feathered Forest detachment.

sentences.zh: 高祖末，以征討有功，賜爵晉陽男。

translations.literal: At the end of Gaozu's reign, for campaign merit he was granted Baron of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Gaozu's reign his campaigns won him Baron of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 累遷領軍、畿部都督。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Director of the Guards and metropolitan-area commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Guards and commander of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 武泰元年，尒朱榮至河陰，殺戮朝士，鷙與榮共登高冢俯而觀之，自此後與榮合。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wutai, Erzhu Rong reached Heyin and slaughtered court gentlemen; Zhi with Rong together climbed a high mound and looked down—from then on he joined with Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In Wutai year one Erzhu Rong came to Heyin and butchered the court; Zhi climbed a mound beside him to watch the killing, and afterward threw in his lot with Rong.

sentences.zh: 元顥之逼也，鷙從駕北迎。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed close, Zhi followed the emperor north to welcome support.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao closed in, Zhi rode north with the emperor to meet relief.

sentences.zh: 既到河內，欲入城，鷙奏曰：「河內晝則閉門，夜引駕入，此之意趣，難以測量。

translations.literal: Having reached Henei and wishing to enter the city, Zhi memorialized: "Henei by day closes its gates and by night would lead Your Majesty in—the meaning of this is hard to measure.
translations.idiomatic: At Henei, when the emperor wished to enter the city, Zhi memorialized: "By day its gates stay shut and by night they would admit you—such intentions are impossible to read.

sentences.zh: 本圖有在，願便發邁。

translations.literal: Your original plan has its purpose; I beg you set out at once."
translations.idiomatic: Your design still holds; I urge you to march on at once."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，前至長子，以尒朱榮赴援，除鷙車騎將軍，封華山王。

translations.literal: The emperor assented; they advanced first to Changzi; because Erzhu Rong came to rescue, Zhi was made General of Agile Cavalry and enfeoffed Prince of Huashan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and pushed on to Changzi; when Erzhu Rong came to the rescue, Zhi was made General of Agile Cavalry and Prince of Huashan.

sentences.zh: 莊帝既殺尒朱榮，榮從子兆為亂，帝欲率諸軍親討，鷙與兆陰通，乃勸帝曰：「黃河萬仞，寧可卒渡。

translations.literal: After Emperor Zhuang had killed Erzhu Rong, Rong's clansman Zhao made disorder; the emperor wished to lead the armies in person to campaign; Zhi had secret communication with Zhao and urged the emperor, "The Yellow River is ten thousand ren deep—how could you cross it in haste?"
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhuang killed Erzhu Rong, Rong's kinsman Zhao rose in revolt; the emperor meant to take the field himself, but Zhi was in secret with Zhao and urged him, "The Yellow River is ten thousand ren deep—will you ford it in haste?"

sentences.zh: 」帝遂自安。

translations.literal: The emperor then composed himself in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took ease and stayed put.

sentences.zh: 及兆入殿，鷙又約止衞兵。

translations.literal: When Zhao entered the hall, Zhi also arranged to restrain the guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao entered the hall Zhi also held back the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 帝見逼，京邑破，皆由鷙之謀。

translations.literal: The emperor was pressed, the capital broke—all through Zhi's plotting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was cornered and the capital fell—all by Zhi's design.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，入為大司馬，加侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing he entered office as Grand Marshal with added attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaojing he entered court as Grand Marshal with the added rank of attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 鷙有武藝，木訥少言，性方厚，每息直省闥，雖暑月不解衣冠。

translations.literal: Zhi had martial skill, was wooden in speech and few of words, and his nature was square and generous; each time he rested on duty at the palace gate, even in hot summer he did not remove cap and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was a fighter, slow of tongue and sparing of words, but upright and steady; on gate duty in midsummer he would not loosen cap or gown.

sentences.zh: 曾於侍中高岳之席，咸陽王坦恃力使酒，陵侮一坐，眾皆下之，不敢應答。

translations.literal: Once at Attendant-in-Chief Gao Yue's feast, Prince of Xianyang Tan relied on strength and drank wine, bullying the whole company; all lowered themselves and dared not answer.
translations.idiomatic: At a feast of Attendant-in-Chief Gao Yue, Prince of Xianyang Tan, drunk on his strength, bullied the table until every man shrank silent.

sentences.zh: 坦謂鷙曰：「孔雀老武官，何因得王？

translations.literal: Tan said to Zhi, "Peacock, you old military officer—why did you get to be prince?"
translations.idiomatic: Tan said to Zhi, "Peacock, you old soldier—how did you become a prince?"

sentences.zh: 」鷙即答曰：「斬反人元禧首，是以得之。

translations.literal: Zhi at once answered, "I cut off the rebel Yuan Xi's head—that is how I got it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi answered at once, "I took the rebel Yuan Xi's head—that is how."

sentences.zh: 」眾皆失色，鷙怡然如故。

translations.literal: All turned pale; Zhi was at ease as before.
translations.idiomatic: The room went white; Zhi sat easy as ever.

sentences.zh: 興和三年薨，贈假黃鉞、尚書令、司徒公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xinghe he died; posthumously granted acting yellow battle-axe, Masters of Writing director, and Duke of the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Xinghe and was posthumously given acting yellow battle-axe, director of the Masters of Writing, and Duke of the Masses.

sentences.zh: 子大器，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Daqi inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daqi inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 後與元瑾謀害齊文襄王，見害。

translations.literal: Later, with Yuan Jin he plotted to harm Prince Wenxiang of Qi and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Yuan Jin in a plot against Prince Wenxiang of Qi and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 孤孫度，太祖初賜爵松滋侯，位比部尚書。

translations.literal: Gu's grandson Du—in early Taizu was granted Marquis of Songzi and held office as director of comparative review in the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Gu's grandson Du, enfeoffed Marquis of Songzi under early Taizu, served as director of comparative review.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子乙斤，襲爵襄陽侯。

translations.literal: His son Yijin inherited Marquis of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yijin took up Marquis of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 顯祖崇舊齒，拜外都大官，甚見優重。

translations.literal: Xianzu honored old worthies, appointed him chief official of the outer court, and greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu, honoring his years, made him chief of the outer court and treated him with great weight.

sentences.zh: 卒

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子平，字楚國，襲世爵松滋侯。

translations.literal: His son Ping, styled Chuguo, inherited the hereditary Marquis of Songzi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ping, styled Chuguo, inherited the hereditary marquisate of Songzi.

sentences.zh: 以軍功賜艾陵男。

translations.literal: For military merit he was granted Baron of Ailing.
translations.idiomatic: Battle honors won him Baron of Ailing.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子萇，高祖時，襲爵松滋侯，例降侯，賜艾陵伯。

translations.literal: His son Chang—in Gaozu's time inherited Marquis of Songzi; as a rule he was reduced from marquis and granted Baron of Ailing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang inherited Songzi under Gaozu but, by the usual rule, was demoted from marquis to Baron of Ailing.

sentences.zh: 萇性剛毅，雖有吉慶事，未嘗開口而笑。

translations.literal: Chang's nature was firm and unyielding; though there were auspicious and celebratory affairs he never opened his mouth to laugh.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was iron by nature; even at weddings and feasts he never smiled.

sentences.zh: 高祖遷都，萇以代尹留鎮。

translations.literal: When Gaozu moved the capital, Chang as acting chief of Dai stayed behind to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu moved the capital, Chang stayed behind as acting chief of Dai to hold the north.

sentences.zh: 除懷朔鎮都大將，因別賜萇酒，雖拜飲，而顏色不泰。

translations.literal: He was removed and made commander-in-chief of Huaishuo garrison; separately granted Chang wine—though he bowed and drank, his complexion was not peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commander at Huaishuo; Gaozu sent him wine apart from the court, and though he bowed and drank, his face never eased.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「聞公一生不笑，今方隔山，[3]當為朕笑。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "I hear that you never laugh all your life—now we are separated by mountains, [3] you ought to laugh for me."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "They tell me you have never laughed in all your days—now mountains lie between us, [3] so laugh once for me."

sentences.zh: 」竟不能得。

translations.literal: Still he could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Even so Chang would not smile.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「五行之氣，偏有所不入。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Of the five phases' qi, some places partly do not enter."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Among the five phases, some temperaments never take a given element."

sentences.zh: 六合之間，亦何事不有。

translations.literal: Between the six directions, is there anything that does not exist?"
translations.idiomatic: "Under heaven, what wonder does not exist?"

sentences.zh: 」左右見者，無不扼腕大笑。

translations.literal: Those attending nearby all clutched their wrists and laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants clutched their sides and roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，為北中郎將，帶河內太守。

translations.literal: In Shizong's time he was northern central army general with concurrent Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong he was northern central army general and concurrent Administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 萇以河橋船絙路狹，不便行旅，又秋水汎漲，年常破壞，乃為船路，遂廣募空車從京出者，[4]率令輸石一雙，累以為岸。

translations.literal: Chang thought the He Bridge mooring road was narrow and inconvenient for travelers; also autumn waters flooded yearly and often destroyed it, so he made a boat route and broadly recruited empty carts leaving the capital, [4] ordering each in turn to haul one pair of stones, piling them to form banks.
translations.idiomatic: Chang found the He Bridge towpath too narrow for traffic and the autumn floods too ruinous, so he opened a boat channel and pressed every empty cart leaving the capital [4] to haul a load of stone until banks rose on either side.

sentences.zh: 橋闊，來往便利，近橋諸郡，無復勞擾，公私賴之。

translations.literal: The bridge widened and coming and going were convenient; commanderies near the bridge had no more forced labor and disturbance; public and private relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: The crossing widened, travel eased, and neighboring commanderies were spared the old corvée; public and private alike prospered by it.

sentences.zh: 歷位度支尚書、侍中、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He held office as director of revenue, attendant-in-ordinary, and Inspector of Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of revenue, attendant-in-ordinary, and Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰成。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was styled Cheng.

sentences.zh: 萇中年以後，官位微達，乃自尊倨，閨門無禮，昆季不穆，性又貪虐，論者鄙之。

translations.literal: After mid-life Chang's office and rank were slightly attained and then he became arrogant and self-important; within the gates there was no propriety, brothers were not harmonious, and his nature was also greedy and cruel; commentators despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Only in middle age did Chang's modest offices ripen into pride: at home he abandoned ritual, quarreled with his kin, and grew greedy and harsh, and men of judgment scorned him.

sentences.zh: 萇子子華，字伏榮，襲爵。

translations.literal: Chang's son Zihua, styled Furong, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's son Zihua, styled Furong, took up the fief.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，除齊州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang he was appointed Inspector of Qi province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Zhuang's reign he became Inspector of Qi.

sentences.zh: 先是，州境數經反逆，邢杲之亂，人不自保。

translations.literal: Before this, the province's territory had repeatedly seen rebellion; in Xing Tuo's disorder people could not protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The province had long been torn by revolt; in Xing Tuo's rising no one could keep himself safe.

sentences.zh: 而子華撫集豪右，委之管籥，眾皆感悅，境內帖然。

translations.literal: Yet Zihua gathered and settled powerful families, entrusted them with authority—the multitude all were moved and pleased; within the borders were calm.
translations.idiomatic: Zihua rallied the great clans, gave them authority, and won their hearts until the land lay quiet.

sentences.zh: 而性甚褊急，當其急也，口不擇言，手自捶擊。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was very narrow and urgent; when urgent he did not choose words in his mouth and with his own hand would strike and beat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was quick-tempered: in a rage he spoke without restraint and struck out with his own fists.

sentences.zh: 長史鄭子湛，子華親友也，見侮罵，遂即去之。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Zheng Zihan was Zihua's close friend yet was insulted and reviled and at once left him.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk and friend Zheng Zihan bore his abuse once too often and walked away.

sentences.zh: 子華雖自悔厲，終不能改。

translations.literal: Zihua, though he repented and exerted himself, still could not change.
translations.idiomatic: Zihua repented and strained to reform, but the habit held.

sentences.zh: 在官不為矯潔之行，凡有餽贈者，辭多受少，故人不厭其取。

translations.literal: In office he did not perform hypocritical acts; whenever there were gifts, he mostly declined much and accepted little, so men did not resent his taking.
translations.idiomatic: He never played the hypocrite in office: when gifts came he refused the bulk and took little, so men did not begrudge him.

sentences.zh: 鞠獄訊囚，務加仁恕。

translations.literal: In judging cases and examining prisoners he strove to add benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: In trials he leaned toward mercy.

sentences.zh: 齊人樹碑頌德。

translations.literal: The people of Qi set up a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qi raised a stele to his virtue.

sentences.zh: 後除濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was removed and made Inspector of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to Inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆之入洛也，齊州城人趙洛周逐刺史丹陽王蕭贊，表濟南太守房士達攝行州事。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, the people of Qi province Zhao Luozhou drove out Inspector Prince of Danyang Xiao Zan and memorialized Administrator of Jinan Fang Shida to act as provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao took Luoyang, Zhao Luozhou of Qi drove out Inspector Xiao Zan, Prince of Danyang, and asked Jinan Administrator Fang Shida to govern the province.

sentences.zh: 洛周子元顯先隨子華在濟州，邀路改表，請子華復為齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Luozhou's son Yuanxian had first followed Zihua at Ji province; he intercepted the road and changed the memorial, asking that Zihua again be Inspector of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou's son Yuanxian, who had served under Zihua in Ji, waylaid the dispatch and rewrote it to restore Zihua to Qi.

sentences.zh: 子華母房氏，曾就親人飲食，夜還大吐，人以為中毒，甚憂懼，子華遂掬吐盡噉之，其母乃安。

translations.literal: Zihua's mother the Fang clan had once gone to a relative's for food and drink; returning at night she vomited greatly; people thought she had been poisoned and were very worried, but Zihua then scooped up the vomit, ate it all, and his mother was then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zihua's mother, Lady Fang, fell violently ill after a relative's feast; fearing poison, the household panicked until Zihua ate her vomit and she recovered her ease.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂還都。

translations.literal: Soon, because of mourning for his mother, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left for the capital in mourning for her.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，除南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing he was appointed Inspector of southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaojing he was made Inspector of southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 弟子思通使關西，朝廷使右衞將軍郭瓊收之。

translations.literal: His younger brother's son Zisi was sent as envoy to Guanxi; the court sent Right Guard General Guo Qiong to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zisi was sent to Guanxi; the court dispatched Right Guard General Guo Qiong to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 子思謂瓊僕曰：「速可見殺，何為久執國士！

translations.literal: Zisi said to Qiong's servant, "Quickly kill me—why long hold a man of the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Zisi told Qiong's man, "Kill me now—why keep a servant of the realm in bonds?"

sentences.zh: 」子華謂子思曰：「由汝粗疏，令我如此。

translations.literal: Zihua said to Zisi, "Because of your coarse carelessness you have made me thus."
translations.idiomatic: Zihua cried to Zisi, "Your rashness has brought me to this."

sentences.zh: 」以頭叩牀，涕泣不自勝。

translations.literal: He knocked his head on the bed, weeping beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: He beat his head on the bed and wept without restraint.

sentences.zh: 子思以手捋鬚，顧謂子華曰：「君惡體氣。

translations.literal: Zisi stroked his beard with his hand, turned and said to Zihua, "Sir, your breath is ill."
translations.idiomatic: Zisi smoothed his beard and told Zihua, "You have a sour stomach."

sentences.zh: 」尋與子思俱死於門下外省。

translations.literal: Soon both Zisi and he died at the outer office below the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon both men were killed in the outer office below the gate.

sentences.zh: 子思，字眾念，性剛暴，恒以忠烈自許。

translations.literal: Zisi, styled Zhongnian, was by nature fierce and violent and always took loyalty and ardor as his boast.
translations.idiomatic: Zisi, styled Zhongnian, was fierce by nature and prided himself on fierce loyalty.

sentences.zh: 元天穆當朝權，以親從薦為御史中尉。

translations.literal: When Yuan Tianmu held court power, through kin and follower he was recommended as chief rectifier of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuan Tianmu held power he entered the Censorate as chief rectifier through family ties.

sentences.zh: 先是，兼尚書僕射元順奏，以尚書百揆之本，至於公事，不應送御史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuan Shun, acting Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, memorialized that the Masters of Writing are the root of the hundred offices and that official business ought not to be sent to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Yuan Shun, acting vice director of the Masters of Writing, argued that since that office is the root of government, routine business should not be routed to the censors.

sentences.zh: [5]至子思，奏曰：

translations.literal: [5] When Zisi took office, he memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: [5] When Zisi came into the post, he submitted a memorial that said:

sentences.zh: 案御史令云：「中尉督司百僚；

translations.literal: I find in the Censorate statutes: "The Director supervises the hundred offices;
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate regulations state: "The Director oversees the hundred offices;

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史糾察禁內。

translations.literal: the Palace Clerk for Drafting impeaches and investigates within the forbidden precinct."
translations.idiomatic: the drafting clerk investigates misconduct inside the palace."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「中尉出行，車輻前驅，除道一里，王公百辟避路。

translations.literal: "It also states: "When the Director goes abroad, the hub of his carriage leads the way and the road is cleared for one li; kings, dukes, and the hundred ranks yield the road."
translations.idiomatic: "They also say that when the Director travels abroad, his carriage hub goes before him, the road is cleared for a li, and kings, dukes, and all ranks step aside."

sentences.zh: 」時經四帝，前後中尉二十許人，奉以周旋，未曾暫廢。

translations.literal: That statute endured through four emperors; some twenty Directors in succession observed it in turn and it was never even briefly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Four reigns had passed; some twenty directors in succession had lived by that rule, and it had never lapsed even briefly.

sentences.zh: 府寺臺省，並從此令。

translations.literal: The ministries, directorates, terraces, and secretariats all followed this statute.
translations.idiomatic: Every ministry, directorate, terrace, and secretariat followed it.

sentences.zh: 唯肅宗之世，為臨洮舉哀，故兼尚書左僕射臣順不肯與名，又不送簿。

translations.literal: Only in Emperor Xiaozong's time, when mourning was held for Lintao, did the acting Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, my lord Shun, refuse to supply his name and also refuse to send the register.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Emperor Xiaozong, during mourning for Lintao, had the acting left vice director Shun refused to list his name or send the attendance register.

sentences.zh: 故中尉臣酈道元舉而奏之，而順復啟云：「尚書百揆之本，令僕納言之貴，不宜下隸中尉，送名御史。

translations.literal: The former Director Li Daoyuan impeached and memorialized this, whereupon Shun again petitioned, saying, "The Masters of Writing are the root of the hundred offices; the Vice Directors are nobles who present counsel and ought not to be subordinated to the Director and have their names sent to the Censorate."
translations.idiomatic: The former Director Li Daoyuan reported him; Shun answered with another petition: "The Masters of Writing are the root of government; vice directors who speak for the throne should not be made subordinates of the Director and have their names delivered to the Censorate."

sentences.zh: 」尋亦蒙敕，聽如其奏。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he also received an edict approving his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 從此迄今，使無準一。

translations.literal: From then until now there has been no single standard.
translations.idiomatic: Since then there had been no single standard.

sentences.zh: 臣初上臺，具見其事，意欲申請決議，但以權兼，未宜便爾。

translations.literal: When I first entered the terrace I saw the affair in full and meant to petition for a binding decision, but because my post was concurrent I thought it premature to act at once.
translations.idiomatic: When I first took my seat on the terrace I saw the whole affair and meant to petition for a firm ruling, but my post was only concurrent and I hesitated to move too soon.

sentences.zh: 日復一日，遂歷炎涼。

translations.literal: Day piled on day until hot and cold seasons had turned.
translations.idiomatic: Days became months until seasons had turned.

sentences.zh: 去月朔旦，臺移尚書索應朝名帳，而省稽留不送。

translations.literal: On the first day of last month the terrace sent notice to the Masters of Writing demanding the attendance roster for court, but the secretariat delayed and would not send it.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of last month the terrace asked the Masters of Writing for the court attendance roster; the secretariat held it back.

sentences.zh: 尋復移催并主吏，忽為尚書郎中裴獻伯後注云：「案舊事，御史中尉逢臺郎於複道，中尉下車執板，郎中車上舉手禮之。

translations.literal: Soon another notice pressed them and named the chief clerk; suddenly a marginal note by Pei Xianbo, a gentleman of the Masters of Writing, read, "According to precedent, when the Director of the Censorate meets a terrace gentleman in the covered passage, the Director alights and holds his tablet while the gentleman on the carriage raises his hand in salute.
translations.idiomatic: A second demand named the chief clerk; then Pei Xianbo, a gentleman of the Masters of Writing, added a marginal note: "By old precedent, when the Director meets a terrace gentleman in the covered passage, the Director dismounts with his tablet while the gentleman salutes from the carriage."

sentences.zh: 以此而言，明非敵體。

translations.literal: From this it is clear they are not equals."
translations.idiomatic: That shows they are not equals."

sentences.zh: 」臣既見此，深為怪愕。

translations.literal: When I saw this I was deeply astonished.
translations.idiomatic: I was astonished when I read it.

sentences.zh: 旋省二三，未解所以。

translations.literal: I turned the matter over two or three times and could not understand the reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: I turned it over again and again and could not see the reasoning.

sentences.zh: 正謂都省別被新式，改易高祖舊命，即遣移問，事何所依。

translations.literal: I supposed the secretariat had separately received some new form and had altered Emperor Gaozu's old command, so I sent notice asking on what authority the matter rested.
translations.idiomatic: I assumed the secretariat had received some new rule and set aside Emperor Gaozu's old order, and sent notice asking what authority they relied on.

sentences.zh: 又獲尚書郎中王元旭報，出蔡氏漢官，似非穿鑿。

translations.literal: I also received a reply from Wang Yuanxu, another gentleman of the Masters of Writing, citing Cai Yong's Han Offices—it did not seem forced.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanxu, another gentleman of the Masters of Writing, answered with a passage from Cai Yong's Han Offices; it did not look far-fetched.

sentences.zh: 始知裴、王亦規壞典謨，兩人心欲自矯。

translations.literal: Then I knew that Pei and Wang both meant to break the statutes; each wished to justify himself.
translations.idiomatic: Then I understood that Pei and Wang meant to break the statutes—each trying to excuse himself.

sentences.zh: 臣案漢書宣秉傳云，詔徵秉為御史中丞，與司隸校尉、尚書令俱會殿庭，並專席而坐，京師號之為三獨坐。

translations.literal: I find in the Han shu biography of Xuan Bing that an edict summoned Bing as Director of the Censorate; he and the Director of the Secretariat Police and the Director of the Masters of Writing met in the palace hall, each with a separate seat, and the capital called them the Three Who Sit Alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Han shu biography of Xuan Bing records an edict summoning him as Director of the Censorate; he met in the hall with the Director of the Secretariat Police and the Director of the Masters of Writing, each with his own seat—the capital called them the Three Who Sit Alone.

sentences.zh: 又尋魏書崔琰傳、晉文陽□傅嘏傳，皆云既為中丞，百僚震悚。

translations.literal: I also searched the Wei shu biography of Cui Yan and the Jin biography of Fu Gu of Wenyang [one graph deficient in the source]; both say that once he became Director, the hundred offices trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: I also searched the Wei shu life of Cui Yan and the Jin life of Fu Gu of Wenyang, where one character is lost in the source; both say that once he was Director the hundred offices trembled.

sentences.zh: [6]以此而言，則中丞不揖省郎蓋已久矣，憲臺不屬都堂，亦非今日。

translations.literal: [6] From this it is clear that the Director has not bowed to secretariat gentlemen for a long time, and that the Censorate does not belong to the secretariat—this is not a matter of today alone.
translations.idiomatic: [6] So the Director has not bowed to secretariat gentlemen in a long time, and the Censorate has never belonged to the secretariat—none of this began yesterday.

sentences.zh: 又尋職令云：「朝會失時，即加彈糾。

translations.literal: I also find in the office statutes: "If one is late for court assembly, impeachment and censure follow at once."
translations.idiomatic: The office statutes also say: "Late arrival at court is impeached on the spot."

sentences.zh: 」則百官簿帳，應送上臺，灼然明矣。

translations.literal: Then the registers of the hundred offices ought to be sent up to the terrace—this is plainly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Registers of the hundred offices must therefore be sent to the terrace—plain as daylight.

sentences.zh: 又皇太子以下違犯憲制，皆得糾察，則令僕朝名宜付御史，又亦彰矣。

translations.literal: Again, violations of the statutes by the crown prince and below may all be investigated and censured; then the Vice Directors' names for court ought to be delivered to the Censorate—this too is obvious.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone from the crown prince down who breaks the statutes may be investigated; vice directors' court names should go to the Censorate—equally obvious.

sentences.zh: 不付名至，否臧何驗？

translations.literal: If names are not delivered, by what proof are good and ill judged?
translations.idiomatic: Without those names, how is merit or fault to be judged?

sentences.zh: 臣順專執，未為平通，先朝曲遂，豈是正法？

translations.literal: Shun's stubborn insistence is not fair and even; that the former court indulged him—is that proper law?
translations.idiomatic: Shun's stubbornness is not equitable; that the previous court indulged him was not proper law.

sentences.zh: 謹案尚書郎中臣裴獻伯、王元旭等，望班士流，早參清宦，輕弄短札，斐然若斯，苟執異端，忽焉至此，此而不綱，將隳朝令。

translations.literal: I respectfully find that the gentlemen of the Masters of Writing Pei Xianbo, Wang Yuanxu, and others, though they stand among the elite and entered pure office early, lightly toyed with brief notes to this shining effect; clinging to heterodox views they suddenly reached this pass—if this is not disciplined, court commands will be ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xianbo, Wang Yuanxu, and the rest stand among the elite and entered pure office early, yet they toyed with brief notes to this effect; clinging to perverse views they have come to this—if this goes unpunished, court orders will collapse.

sentences.zh: 請以見事免獻伯等所居官，付法科處。

translations.literal: I ask that, on the evidence before us, Xianbo and the rest be removed from their posts and handed to the penal offices.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Xianbo and the others be removed from office on the evidence before us and handed to the penal offices.

sentences.zh: 尚書納言之本，令僕百揆之要，同彼浮虛，助之乖失，宜明首從，節級其罪。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing are the root of presenting counsel; the Vice Directors are the pivot of the hundred offices—like empty vanity they aid this perverse error; the ringleaders should be made plain and their crimes graded by degree.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing are the root of counsel and the vice directors the pivot of government; aiding this error is empty vanity—the ringleaders should be named and punished by degree.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「國異政，不可據之古事。

translations.literal: The edict said, "States differ in government; one cannot rely on ancient affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered: "States differ in government; ancient precedents cannot decide this.

sentences.zh: 付司檢高祖舊格，推處得失以聞。

translations.literal: Hand the matter to the relevant office to examine Emperor Gaozu's old regulations, weigh gain and loss, and report."
translations.idiomatic: Let the relevant office examine Emperor Gaozu's old regulations, weigh the rights and wrongs, and report."

sentences.zh: 」尋從子思奏。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Zisi's memorial was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the court followed Zisi's memorial.

sentences.zh: 仍為元天穆所忿，遂停。

translations.literal: Still Yuan Tianmu resented it, and the matter was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tianmu, resentful, blocked it anyway.

sentences.zh: 元顥之敗，封安定縣子。

translations.literal: After Yuan Hao's defeat he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao's defeat he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Anding.

sentences.zh: 孝靜時，位侍中而死。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaojing he reached Attendant-in-Ordinary and died.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaojing he rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary and died.

sentences.zh: 萇弟珍字金雀，襲爵艾陵男。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Zhen, courtesy name Golden Sparrow, inherited the title Baron of Ailing.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Zhen, courtesy name Golden Sparrow, inherited the barony of Ailing.

sentences.zh: [7]世宗時，曲事高肇，遂為帝寵昵。

translations.literal: [7] Under Emperor Shizong he curried favor with Gao Zhao and so won the emperor's intimate trust.
translations.idiomatic: [7] Under Emperor Shizong he curried favor with Gao Zhao and won the emperor's intimate trust.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰之死，珍率壯士害之。

translations.literal: When Prince of Pengcheng Xie died, Zhen led stalwart men to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Pengcheng Xie died, Zhen led strong men to kill him.

sentences.zh: 後卒於尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Later he died while Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He later died as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 平弟長生，位游、騎擊將軍。

translations.literal: Ping's younger brother Changsheng held the posts of General of the Mobile Corps and Striking Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's younger brother Changsheng was General of the Mobile Corps and Striking Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 孝莊時，以子天穆貴盛，贈司空。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang, because his son Tianmu was powerful, he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang, because his son Tianmu had grown powerful, he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 天穆，性和厚，美形貌，善射，有能名。

translations.literal: Tianmu's nature was mild and generous; he had a handsome face, was skilled at archery, and had a name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu was mild and open-handed, handsome, skilled with the bow, and known for ability.

sentences.zh: 年二十，起家員外郎。

translations.literal: At twenty he first left home to serve as supernumerary gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he entered service as a supernumerary gentleman.

sentences.zh: 六鎮之亂，尚書令李崇、廣陽王深北討，天穆奉使慰勞諸軍。

translations.literal: When the Six Garrisons rebelled, Li Chong, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Guangyang Shen marched north to punish them; Tianmu was sent on mission to comfort the armies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Six Garrisons rebellion, Li Chong, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Guangyang Shen marched north; Tianmu was sent to comfort the troops.

sentences.zh: 路出秀容，尒朱榮見其法令齊整，有將領氣，深相結託，約為兄弟。

translations.literal: Passing through Xiurong, Erzhu Rong saw that his orders were orderly and that he had the air of a commander; they formed a deep bond and swore brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Xiurong, Erzhu Rong saw his commands in good order and a commander's bearing; they bonded deeply and swore brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 未幾，榮請天穆為行臺，朝廷不許，改授別將，令赴秀容。

translations.literal: Before long Rong asked that Tianmu be made mobile-office commissioner; the court did not agree and instead appointed him separate commander, ordering him to proceed to Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Rong asked that Tianmu be made mobile-office commissioner; the court refused and made him a separate commander bound for Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 是時，北鎮紛亂，所在蜂起，六鎮蕩然，無復蕃捍，惟榮當職路衝，招聚散亡。

translations.literal: At that time the northern garrisons were in turmoil and uprisings flared everywhere; the Six Garrisons were swept away with no border defense left—only Rong stood on the main road, gathering the scattered and the lost.
translations.idiomatic: The north was in chaos; the Six Garrisons were gone and the border undefended—only Rong, on the main road, gathered wanderers.

sentences.zh: 天穆為榮腹心，除并州刺史。

translations.literal: Tianmu was Rong's confidant and was made Regional Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu was Rong's confidant and was made regional inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及榮赴洛，天穆參其始謀，乃令天穆留後，為之繼援。

translations.literal: When Rong went to Luoyang, Tianmu took part in the first plot; Rong then left Tianmu behind as rear guard to support him.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong marched on Luoyang Tianmu helped plot the move; Rong left him behind as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 莊帝踐阼，天穆以榮之眷昵，特除太尉，封上黨王，徵赴京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang ascended the throne, Tianmu, through Rong's favor, was specially made Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Prince of Shangdang, and summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaozhuang's accession, through Rong's favor, Tianmu was made Grand Commandant and Prince of Shangdang and summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 榮之討葛榮，詔天穆為前軍都督，率京師之眾以赴之。

translations.literal: When Rong campaigned against Ge Rong, an edict made Tianmu front-army commander-in-chief, leading the capital host to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong campaigned against Ge Rong, an edict made Tianmu commander of the van with the capital armies.

sentences.zh: 榮擒葛榮，天穆增封，通前三萬戶。

translations.literal: When Rong captured Ge Rong, Tianmu's fief was increased to thirty thousand households in all with his prior grants.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong captured Ge Rong, Tianmu's fief rose to thirty thousand households in all, counting earlier grants.

sentences.zh: 尋監國史，錄尚書事，開府，世襲并州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he supervised the national history, recorded Masters of Writing affairs, opened a government office, and hereditarily held Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he supervised the national history, recorded Masters of Writing affairs, opened a government office, and held Bingzhou in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 初，杜洛周、鮮于脩禮為寇，瀛冀諸州人多避亂南向。

translations.literal: Earlier Du Luozhou and Xianyu Xiuli had raided; many in Ying and Ji provinces fled south to escape the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Du Luozhou and Xianyu Xiuli had raided, and many in Ying and Ji fled south.

sentences.zh: 幽州前北平府主簿河間邢杲，[8]擁率部曲，屯據鄚城，以拒洛周、葛榮，垂將三載。

translations.literal: Xing Gao of Hejian, former chief clerk of the former Northern Ping prefecture, [8] led his followers and held Moying city against Luozhou and Ge Rong for nearly three years.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Gao of Hejian, [8] former chief clerk of Northern Ping, led his band and held Moying against Luozhou and Ge Rong for nearly three years.

sentences.zh: 及廣陽王深等敗後，杲南渡居青州北海界。

translations.literal: After Prince of Guangyang Shen and the others were defeated, Gao crossed south and settled on the border of Beihai in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Shen, Prince of Guangyang, was defeated, Gao went south and settled on the Beihai border in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 靈太后詔流人所在皆置命屬郡縣，選豪右為守令以撫鎮之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered that wherever refugees gathered, commandery and county jurisdiction should be assigned and local magnates chosen as administrators to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered refugees registered to commanderies and counties, with local magnates as administrators to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 時青州刺史元世儁表置新安郡，以杲為太守，未報。

translations.literal: Then Regional Inspector of Qingzhou Yuan Shijun memorialized to establish Xin'an commandery with Gao as administrator; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector of Qingzhou Yuan Shijun asked to create Xin'an commandery and make Gao administrator; no reply came.

sentences.zh: 會臺申汰簡所授郡縣，[9]以杲從子子瑤資蔭居前，乃授河間太守。

translations.literal: When the terrace reviewed appointments to commanderies and counties, [9] because Gao's nephew Ziyao ranked higher by inherited privilege, the post of Administrator of Hejian was given instead.
translations.idiomatic: When the terrace reviewed county appointments, [9] Gao's nephew Ziyao ranked higher by inherited privilege and received Hejian instead.

sentences.zh: 杲深耻恨，於是遂反。

translations.literal: Gao was deeply shamed and angry, and thereupon rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was shamed to the bone and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 所在流人先為土人凌忽，聞杲起逆，率來從之，旬朔之間，眾踰十萬。

translations.literal: Refugees who had long been bullied by locals heard Gao had risen and flocked to him; within a month and a half his host passed a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees long bullied by locals heard and joined him; within a month his force passed a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 劫掠村塢，毒害民人，齊人號之為「𦧟榆賊」。

translations.literal: They plundered hamlets and harmed the people; the people of Qi called them the "Bald-elm bandits."
translations.idiomatic: They looted villages and harmed civilians; Qi people called them the Bald-elm Bandits.

sentences.zh: 先是，河南人常笑河北人好食榆葉，故因以號之。

translations.literal: Earlier men of Henan had often mocked men of Hebei for eating elm leaves, and so the name was taken from that.
translations.idiomatic: Henan men had mocked Hebei men for eating elm leaves—hence the nickname.

sentences.zh: 杲東掠光州，盡海而還。

translations.literal: Gao raided east into Guang province, reaching the sea before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Gao raided east into Guang province to the sea and back.

sentences.zh: 又破都督李叔仁軍。

translations.literal: He also defeated the army of Area Commander Li Shuren.
translations.idiomatic: He also broke the army of Area Commander Li Shuren.

sentences.zh: 詔天穆與齊獻武王討大破之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Tianmu and the Prince of Qi, King of Qi Xianwu, to campaign and smash them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Tianmu and the King of Qi Xianwu to crush them.

sentences.zh: 杲乃請降，傳送京師，斬之。

translations.literal: Gao then asked to surrender; he was sent to the capital and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao surrendered, was sent to the capital, and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 增天穆邑萬戶。

translations.literal: Tianmu's fief was increased by ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu's fief grew by ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 時元顥乘虛陷滎陽，天穆聞莊帝北巡，自畢公壘北渡，會車駕於河內。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Hao seized Yingyang while the emperor was exposed; hearing that Emperor Xiaozhuang was touring the north, Tianmu crossed north from Bigong Rampart and met the imperial carriage at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao seized Yingyang; hearing the emperor had gone north, Tianmu crossed from Bigong Rampart and met him at Henei.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮以天時炎熱，欲還師，天穆苦執不可，榮乃從之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong, because the season was fiercely hot, wished to withdraw the army; Tianmu pressed hard that he must not, and Rong yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, finding the heat fierce, wished to withdraw; Tianmu insisted and Rong yielded.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，加太宰，羽葆、鼓吹；

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Tianmu was made Grand Preceptor with feather canopy and martial pipes;
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhuang returned to the palace Tianmu was made Grand Preceptor with feather canopy and martial pipes;

sentences.zh: 增邑，通前七萬戶。

translations.literal: his fief was increased to seventy thousand households in all with prior grants.
translations.idiomatic: his fief rose to seventy thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 天穆以疏屬，本無德望，憑藉尒朱，爵位隆極，當時燻灼，朝野傾悚，王公已下每旦盈門，受納財貨，珍寶充積。

translations.literal: Tianmu was a distant kinsman without real virtue or standing; relying on the Erzhu clan his rank reached the utmost; at the time he blazed so bright that court and country trembled; from kings and dukes down the gate was full every morning as they brought gifts—treasures piled up.
translations.idiomatic: A distant kinsman without standing, he rode the Erzhu to the summit of rank; court and country trembled; kings and dukes packed his gate each dawn with gifts until treasures piled high.

sentences.zh: 而寬柔容物，不甚見疾於時。

translations.literal: Yet he was broad and gentle toward others and was not much hated in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was broad and easy with people and not much hated.

sentences.zh: 莊帝以其榮黨，外示寵敬，詔天穆乘車馬出入大司馬門。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he was Rong's faction, outwardly showed him favor and ordered that Tianmu might enter and leave by the Great Sima Gate in carriage or on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhuang, because he was Rong's man, showed outward favor and let him pass the Great Sima Gate by carriage or horse.

sentences.zh: 天穆與榮相倚，情寄特甚。

translations.literal: Tianmu and Rong leaned on each other; their trust was especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: He and Rong leaned on each other with uncommon trust.

sentences.zh: 榮常以兄禮事之，而尒朱世隆等雖榮子姪，位遇已重，畏憚天穆，俯仰承迎。

translations.literal: Rong always treated him with the rites due an elder brother, while Erzhu Shilong and the rest, though Rong's sons and nephews and already of heavy rank, feared Tianmu and bowed low to please him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong treated him as an elder brother; Shilong and the other Erzhu nephews, though already grandees, feared Tianmu and bowed to please him.

sentences.zh: 天穆曾言世隆之失，榮即加杖，其相親任如此。

translations.literal: When Tianmu once spoke of Shilong's fault, Rong at once had him beaten—their intimacy went that far.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tianmu named Shilong's fault and Rong had Shilong beaten at once—such was their bond.

sentences.zh: 莊帝內畏惡之，與榮同時見殺。

translations.literal: The emperor inwardly feared and hated him; he was killed together with Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared and hated him inwardly; he was killed with Rong.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝初，贈丞相、柱國大將軍、雍州刺史，假黃鉞，諡曰武昭。

translations.literal: At the start of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was posthumously made Chancellor, Pillar General of the State, and Regional Inspector of Yongzhou, with the yellow battle-axe lent, posthumous title Martial-Splendid.
translations.idiomatic: At the Deposed Emperor's accession he was posthumously made Chancellor, pillar general, and regional inspector of Yongzhou, with the yellow battle-axe lent, posthumous name Martial-Splendid.

sentences.zh: 子儼，襲，美才貌。

translations.literal: His son Yi inherited; he had fine talent and looks.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi inherited—talented and handsome.

sentences.zh: 位都官尚書。

translations.literal: He held the post of Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 及齊受禪，聞敕召，假病，遂怖而卒。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate he heard the summons, feigned illness, and died of fright.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate he heard the summons, feigned illness, and died of fear.

sentences.zh: 西河公敦，平文帝之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Duke of Xihe Dun was a great-grandson of Emperor Pingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Xihe Dun was a great-grandson of Emperor Pingwen.

sentences.zh: 太祖初，從征，被堅執銳，名冠諸將。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Taizu's campaigns he followed on campaign, bore hard armor and sharp blades, and his name stood first among the generals.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taizu's wars he followed on campaign in hard mail with a sharp edge, first among the generals.

sentences.zh: 後從征中山，所向無前。

translations.literal: Later he followed the campaign against Zhongshan; wherever he turned none could stand before him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning against Zhongshan, none could stand before him.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，拜中都大官。
