translations.literal: Under Emperor Taizong he was made Grand Palace Steward of the Center.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong he was made Grand Palace Steward of the Center.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，進爵西河公，寵遇彌篤。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Shizu his rank advanced to Duke of Xihe and favor grew still deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu he was advanced to Duke of Xihe and favored still more.

sentences.zh: 卒，子撥襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Bo inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Bo inherited.

sentences.zh: 司徒石，平文帝之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Shi was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Pingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Shi was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Pingwen.

sentences.zh: 忠勇有膽略，尤善騎射。

translations.literal: Loyal and brave with stratagem, he was especially skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal, brave, and resourceful, especially skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 從世祖南討，至瓜步。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Shizu on the southern campaign as far as Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizu south as far as Guabu.

sentences.zh: 位尚書令，雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He held Director of the Masters of Writing and Regional Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was Director of the Masters of Writing and regional inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷比部侍郎、華州刺史，[10]累遷征南大將軍。

translations.literal: He passed through Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Regional Inspector of Hua, [10] and was promoted in succession to General Who Conquers the South.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and regional inspector of Hua, [10] and rose to General Who Conquers the South.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒公。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Duke of Works.

sentences.zh: 武衞將軍謂，烈帝之第四子也。

translations.literal: General of the Martial Guard Wei was the fourth son of Emperor Lie.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Martial Guard Wei was the fourth son of Emperor Lie.

sentences.zh: 寬雅有將略，常從太祖征討有功，除武衞將軍。

translations.literal: Broad and refined with military stratagem, he often followed Emperor Taizu on campaigns with merit and was made General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Broad and refined, with real military grasp, he followed Taizu on campaign with merit and was made General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 後謝老歸家，顯祖善禮遇之，賜几杖服物，致膳於第。

translations.literal: Later he asked leave to retire; Emperor Xianzu treated him with fine courtesy, gave him couch, staff, and robes, and sent meals to his house.
translations.idiomatic: Later he retired; Emperor Xianzu honored him with couch, staff, robes, and meals sent to his house.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜祕器。

translations.literal: He died and was granted secret burial goods.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was granted secret burial goods.

sentences.zh: 子烏真，膂力絕人。

translations.literal: His son Wuzhen had strength beyond other men.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wuzhen had strength beyond other men.

sentences.zh: 隨太祖征伐，屢有戰功，官至鉅鹿太守。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Taizu on campaign he won battle merit again and again and reached Administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Following Taizu he won repeated battle merit and rose to administrator of Julu.

sentences.zh: 子興都，聰敏剛毅。

translations.literal: His son Xingdu was clever, keen, and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xingdu was clever, keen, and hard.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，為河間太守，賜爵樂城子。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Gaozong he was Administrator of Hejian and was granted the title Viscount of Lecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he governed Hejian and was made Viscount of Lecheng.

sentences.zh: 為政嚴猛，百姓憚之。

translations.literal: His government was stern and fierce; the common people feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled sternly and the people feared him.

sentences.zh: 顯祖初，以子丕貴重，進爵樂城侯。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Xianzu's reign, because his son Pi was weighty, his rank was advanced to Marquis of Lecheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzu came to the throne, because his son Pi was eminent, he was advanced to Marquis of Lecheng.

sentences.zh: 謝老歸家，顯祖益禮之，賜几杖服物，致膳於第。

translations.literal: He asked leave to retire; Emperor Xianzu honored him still more, gave couch, staff, and robes, and sent meals to his house.
translations.idiomatic: He retired again; Xianzu honored him further with couch, staff, robes, and meals at his house.

sentences.zh: 其妻婁氏，為東陽王太妃。

translations.literal: His wife, the Lady Lou, was consort-dowager to the Prince of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Lou was consort-dowager to the Prince of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，追贈定州刺史、河間公，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Regional Inspector of Dingzhou and Duke of Hejian, posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made regional inspector of Dingzhou and Duke of Hejian, posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子提，襲父侯爵。

translations.literal: His son Ti inherited his father's marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ti inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 提弟丕，世祖擢拜羽林中郎。

translations.literal: Ti's younger brother Pi was promoted by Emperor Shizu to Gentleman of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Ti's younger brother Pi was promoted by Shizu to Gentleman of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 從駕臨江，賜爵興平子。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor to the river campaign, he was granted the title Viscount of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: On the river campaign he was granted the viscounty of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 顯祖即位，累遷侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu took the throne he was promoted in succession to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzu took the throne he rose in succession to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 丞相乙渾謀反，丕以奏聞。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Yi Hun plotted rebellion, Pi reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Yi Hun plotted treason, Pi reported it.

sentences.zh: 詔丕帥元賀、牛益得收渾，誅之，遷尚書令，改封東陽公。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Pi to lead Yuan He and Niu Yide to seize Hun and execute him; he was moved to Director of the Masters of Writing and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had Pi lead Yuan He and Niu Yide to seize and kill Hun; he became Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，封東陽王，拜侍中、司徒公。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Gaozu he was made Prince of Dongyang and Attendant-in-Ordinary and Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu he was made Prince of Dongyang, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Duke of Works.

sentences.zh: 時有諸疑事三百餘條，敕丕制決，率皆平允。

translations.literal: At that time there were more than three hundred doubtful matters; an edict ordered Pi to decide them; on the whole his judgments were fair.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred doubtful cases were sent to him to decide; his judgments were mostly fair.

sentences.zh: 丕子超生，車駕親幸其第，特加賞賜。

translations.literal: When Pi's son Chao was born the imperial carriage personally visited his house with special rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi's son Chao was born the emperor visited his house with special gifts.

sentences.zh: 以執心不二，詔賜丕入八議，傳示子孫，犯至百，聽責數恕之；

translations.literal: Because his loyalty was undivided, an edict granted Pi entry into the Eight Pardons, to be transmitted to his descendants; for crimes up to a hundred lashes he might be rebuked and forgiven;
translations.idiomatic: For undivided loyalty an edict granted Pi the Eight Pardons for his line: crimes up to a hundred lashes might be rebuked and forgiven;

sentences.zh: 放其同籍丁口雜使役調，永受復除；

translations.literal: the corvée and tax labor of males of his registered household were released forever;
translations.idiomatic: males of his household were forever freed from corvée and tax labor;

sentences.zh: [11]若有姦邪人方便讒毀者，即加斬戮。

translations.literal: [11] if any wicked man should conveniently slander him, that man was to be beheaded at once.
translations.idiomatic: [11] anyone who slandered him by trickery was to be beheaded at once.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太尉、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Grand Commandant and Recorder of Masters of Writing Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Grand Commandant and recorder of Masters of Writing affairs.

sentences.zh: 時淮南王他、淮陽王尉元、河東王苟頹並以舊老見禮，每有大事，引入禁中，乘步挽，杖于朝，進退相隨。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Huainan Ta, Prince of Huaiyang Wei Yuan, and Prince of Hedong Gou Ti were all honored as elders of former times; whenever great affairs arose they were brought into the forbidden precinct, rode in hand-drawn carriages, and leaned on staffs at court, advancing and withdrawing together.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huainan Ta, Prince of Huaiyang Wei Yuan, and Prince of Hedong Gou Ti were honored as elders; on great affairs they entered the palace in hand-drawn carriages with staffs at court, moving together.

sentences.zh: 丕、他、元三人，皆容貌壯偉，腰帶十圍，大耳秀眉，鬚鬢斑白，百僚觀瞻，莫不祗聳。

translations.literal: Pi, Ta, and Yuan—the three of them—were all of imposing build, belts ten spans round, large ears and fine brows, beards and temples grizzled; the hundred offices looked on and none failed to stand in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Pi, Ta, and Yuan were imposing men—belts ten spans round, large ears, fine brows, grizzled beards; officials looked on in awe.

sentences.zh: 唯苟頹小為短劣，姿望亦不逮之。

translations.literal: Only Gou Ti was somewhat shorter and smaller; his bearing and looks did not reach theirs.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gou Ti was shorter; his looks did not match.

sentences.zh: 高祖、文明太后重年敬舊，存問周渥，賜以珍寶。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming valued age and honored the old; they sent frequent inquiries and thick gifts of treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming honored age with frequent visits and rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 丕聲氣高朗，博記國事，饗讌之際，恒居坐端，必抗音大言，敍列既往成敗。

translations.literal: Pi's voice was high and clear; he remembered state affairs broadly; at banquets he always sat at the head and would raise his voice to speak at length, recounting past success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: Pi spoke in a high, clear voice and remembered state affairs; at banquets he sat at the head and recounted past victories and defeats in a ringing voice.

sentences.zh: 帝后敬納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress listened with respect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress listened with respect.

sentences.zh: 然諂事要人，驕侮輕賤，每見王叡、苻承祖，常傾身下之。

translations.literal: Yet he flattered those in power and was arrogant toward the lowly; whenever he saw Wang Rui or Fu Chengzu he would bend his body to place himself below them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he flattered the powerful and despised the lowly; before Wang Rui or Fu Chengzu he bent low.

sentences.zh: 時文明太后為王叡造宅，故亦為丕造甲第。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Wenming built a mansion for Wang Rui, so she also built a first-rank mansion for Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Wenming built a mansion for Wang Rui and likewise a first-rank house for Pi.

sentences.zh: 第成，帝后親幸之，率百官文武饗落焉。

translations.literal: When the house was finished the emperor and empress visited in person and led the hundred civil and military officials to a housewarming feast.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished the emperor and empress visited and feasted the civil and military officials there.

sentences.zh: 使尚書令王叡宣詔，賜丕金印一紐。

translations.literal: Wang Rui, Director of the Masters of Writing, was ordered to proclaim the edict and grant Pi one golden seal-cord.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Rui proclaimed an edict granting Pi one golden seal-cord.

sentences.zh: 太后親造勸戒歌辭以賜羣官，丕上疏贊謝。

translations.literal: The empress dowager personally composed admonitory song-verses and gave them to the officials; Pi submitted a memorial of praise and thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager composed admonitory songs for the officials; Pi thanked her in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 太后令曰：「臣哉隣哉，隣哉臣哉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered, "Ministers, neighbors! Neighbors, ministers!
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Ministers, neighbors! Neighbors, ministers!

sentences.zh: 君則亡逸於上，臣則履冰於下。

translations.literal: The ruler must not idle above; ministers must walk on ice below.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler must not idle above; ministers must walk on ice below.

sentences.zh: 若能如此，太平豈難致乎？

translations.literal: If you can be thus, how hard is great peace to attain?"
translations.idiomatic: If you can be thus, how hard is peace to win?"

sentences.zh: 」及丕妻段氏卒，諡曰恭妃。

translations.literal: When Pi's wife the Lady Duan died she was given the posthumous title Consort Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi's wife Lady Duan died she received the posthumous title Consort Gong.

sentences.zh: 又特賜丕金券。

translations.literal: Pi was also specially granted a golden tally.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was also specially granted a golden tally.

sentences.zh: 高祖、文明太后引見公卿於皇信堂，太后曰：「今京師旱儉，欲聽飢貧之人出關逐食。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming received the dukes and ministers in the Hall of Imperial Trust and the empress dowager said, "Now the capital suffers drought and dearth; I wish to let hungry and poor people leave the passes to seek food elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Wenming received the ministers in the Hall of Imperial Trust; the empress dowager said, "The capital suffers drought and dearth; I wish to let the hungry poor leave the passes to seek food.

sentences.zh: 如欲給過所，恐稽延時日，不救災窘，若任其外出，復慮姦良難辨。

translations.literal: If we issue travel permits I fear days will be lost and the disaster will not be relieved; if we let them go freely I again fear good and wicked will be hard to tell apart.
translations.idiomatic: Travel permits may cost days we do not have; free departure may mix honest folk with rogues.

sentences.zh: 卿等可議其所宜。

translations.literal: You should debate what is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Debate what is fitting."

sentences.zh: 」丕議：「諸曹下大夫以上，人各將二吏，別掌給過所，州郡亦然，不過三日，給之便訖，有何難也？

translations.literal: Pi argued, "Every gentleman of the Masters of Writing from junior clerk upward should each take two clerks and separately manage issuing permits; commanderies and counties likewise—within three days at most issuance would be finished; what difficulty is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Pi said: "Let every Masters of Writing gentleman from junior clerk up take two clerks each to issue permits; let commanderies and counties do the same—in three days it would be done. What difficulty?"

sentences.zh: 」高祖從之，四日而訖。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu followed this; in four days it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu agreed; in four days it was finished.

sentences.zh: 丕請立東宮，詔曰：「年尚幼小，有何急之？

translations.literal: Pi asked to establish the Eastern Palace; the edict said, "The years are still young—what hurry is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Pi asked to establish the crown prince; the edict answered, "He is still young—what hurry?"

sentences.zh: 」丕曰：「臣年在西夕，思觀盛禮，於臣實急。

translations.literal: Pi said, "Your servant's years stand in the western dusk; I long to witness the great rite—for me it is urgent."
translations.idiomatic: Pi said, "My years stand in the western dusk; I long to see the great rite—for me it is urgent."

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: He was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Permission was refused.

sentences.zh: 後例降王爵，封平陽郡公。

translations.literal: Later, by precedent, princely rank was reduced; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by precedent, his princely rank was reduced to Duke of Pingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 求致任，詔不許。

translations.literal: He asked to resign office; the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to resign; the edict refused.

sentences.zh: 及車駕南伐，丕與廣陵王羽留守京師，並加使持節。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Pi and Prince of Guangling Yu remained to guard the capital, both given credential-bearing authority.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south, Pi and Prince of Guangling Yu guarded the capital, both with credential-bearing authority.

sentences.zh: 詔丕、羽曰：「留守非賢莫可。

translations.literal: The edict to Pi and Yu said, "To remain and guard, none but the worthy will do.
translations.idiomatic: The edict to Pi and Yu said, "Only the worthy can guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 太尉年尊德重，位總阿衡；

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant is advanced in years and heavy in virtue; his post sums up the regent's charge;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant is old and weighty in virtue, his post the pivot of government;

sentences.zh: 羽朕之懿弟，溫柔明斷。

translations.literal: Yu is Our splendid younger brother, gentle, warm, clear, and decisive.
translations.idiomatic: Yu is Our splendid younger brother—gentle, warm, clear, and decisive.

sentences.zh: 故使二人留守京邑，授以二節，賞罰在手。

translations.literal: Therefore We send these two to guard the capital city and grant them two credentials with reward and punishment in hand.
translations.idiomatic: We send these two to guard the capital with two credentials and reward and punishment in hand.

sentences.zh: 其祗允成憲，以稱朕心。

translations.literal: Reverently fulfill the established statutes to match Our heart."
translations.idiomatic: Fulfill the statutes faithfully to match Our heart."

sentences.zh: 」丕對曰：「謹以死奉詔。

translations.literal: Pi replied, "I respectfully obey unto death."
translations.idiomatic: Pi answered, "I will obey unto death."

sentences.zh: 」羽對曰：「太尉宜專節度，臣但可副貳而已。

translations.literal: Yu replied, "The Grand Commandant should hold sole command; your servant can only be second."
translations.idiomatic: Yu answered, "The Grand Commandant should command alone; I can only assist."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「老者之智，少者之決，何得辭也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "The old have wisdom; the young have decision—how can you decline?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "The old have wisdom, the young decision—how can you decline?"

sentences.zh: 」及高祖還代，丕請作歌，詔許之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu returned to Dai, Pi asked to compose a song; the edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu returned to Dai, Pi asked to compose a song and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 歌訖，高祖曰：「公傾朕還車，故親歌述志。

translations.literal: When the song was finished Emperor Gaozu said, "You inclined Our returning carriage, so We personally sang to state Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the song was done Gaozu said, "You bent Our returning carriage, so We sang Our intent in person.

sentences.zh: 今經構既有次第，故暫還舊京，願後時亦同茲適。」

translations.literal: Now construction already has its order; We therefore return for a time to the old capital—may later times share this joy as well."
translations.idiomatic: Construction has its order; We return for a time to the old capital—may later days share this joy."

sentences.zh: 及高祖欲遷都，臨太極殿，引見留守之官大議。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu wished to move the capital he came to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, summoned the remaining guard officers, and held great debate.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu wished to move the capital he came to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, summoned the guard officers, and held great debate.

sentences.zh: 乃詔丕等，如有所懷，各陳其志。

translations.literal: He then ordered Pi and the others that if they had thoughts they should each state their will.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Pi and the others each to speak his mind.

sentences.zh: 燕州刺史穆羆進曰：「移都事大，如臣愚見，謂為未可。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector of Yanzhou Mu Ba advanced and said, "The matter of moving the capital is great; in this servant's foolish view it cannot yet be done."
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector of Yanzhou Mu Ba said, "Moving the capital is great; in my foolish view it cannot yet be done."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「卿便言不可之理。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "Then speak the reasons it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Speak the reasons it cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 」羆曰：「北有獫狁之寇，南有荊揚未賓，西有吐谷渾之阻，東有高句麗之難。

translations.literal: Ba said, "In the north are the Xianyun raiders; in the south Jing and Yang are not yet submitted; in the west Tuyuhun blocks the way; in the east Koguryo is hard to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Ba said, "North are Xianyun raiders; south Jing and Yang are unsubmitted; west Tuyuhun blocks; east Koguryo is hard.

sentences.zh: 四方未平，九區未定。

translations.literal: The four quarters are not yet pacified; the nine regions are not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: The four quarters are not pacified; the nine regions unsettled.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，謂為不可。

translations.literal: From this I infer it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: From this I infer it cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 征伐之舉，要須戎馬，如其無馬，事不可克。

translations.literal: Campaigns require war-horses; without horses affairs cannot succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns need war-horses; without horses nothing succeeds."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「卿言無馬，此理粗可。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "Your saying there are no horses is roughly acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Your point about horses is roughly acceptable.

sentences.zh: 馬常出北方，廄在此置，卿何慮無馬？

translations.literal: Horses always come from the north; the stud is placed here—why worry there will be no horses?
translations.idiomatic: Horses come from the north; the stud is here—why fear there will be none?

sentences.zh: 今代在恒山之北，為九州之外，以是之故，遷于中原。

translations.literal: Now Dai lies north of Mount Heng, outside the Nine Provinces; for this reason We move to the central plain."
translations.idiomatic: Dai lies north of Mount Heng, outside the Nine Provinces; for that We move to the central plain."

sentences.zh: 」羆曰：「臣聞黃帝都涿鹿。

translations.literal: Ba said, "I have heard that the Yellow Emperor's capital was at Zhuolu.
translations.idiomatic: Ba said, "I hear the Yellow Emperor's capital was Zhuolu.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，古昔聖王不必悉居中原。

translations.literal: From this, ancient sage kings did not all dwell in the central plain."
translations.idiomatic: So ancient sage kings did not all dwell in the central plain."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「黃帝以天下未定，居于涿鹿，既定之後，亦遷于河南。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "The Yellow Emperor, because the realm was not settled, dwelt at Zhuolu; once it was settled he also moved to Henan."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "The Yellow Emperor dwelt at Zhuolu while the realm was unsettled; once settled he moved to Henan."

sentences.zh: 」尚書于果曰：[12]「臣誠不識古事，如聞百姓之言，先皇建都於此，無何欲移，以為不可。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Yu Guo said: [12] "Your servant truly does not know ancient affairs; as I hear the common people speak, the late emperor built the capital here—suddenly to move, they think it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Yu Guo said: [12] "I truly do not know antiquity; as the people say, the late emperor built here—to move suddenly they think cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 中原其如是所由擬。

translations.literal: The central plain is as they describe for the reasons they imagine.
translations.idiomatic: The central plain is what they imagine it to be.

sentences.zh: [13]數有篡奪。

translations.literal: [13] There have been many usurpations.
translations.idiomatic: [13] There have been many usurpations.

sentences.zh: 自建邑平城以來，與天地並固，日月齊明。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the city at Pingcheng it has been firm as heaven and earth, bright as sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Since Pingcheng was founded it has stood firm as heaven and earth, bright as sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 臣雖管見膚淺，性不昭達，終不以恒代之地，而擬伊洛之美。

translations.literal: Your servant's shallow tube-view and nature not bright and penetrating would never compare the land of Heng and Dai to the beauty of Yiluo.
translations.idiomatic: My shallow sight would never compare Heng and Dai to the beauty of Yiluo.

sentences.zh: 但以安土重遷，物之常性，一旦南移，懼不樂也。

translations.literal: But settling on the soil and honoring migration are the constant nature of things; once moved south in a day, I fear they will not be glad."
translations.idiomatic: Yet honoring the soil and dreading migration are human nature; move south in a day and I fear they will not rejoice."

sentences.zh: 」丕曰：「陛下去歲親御六軍討蕭氏，至洛，遣任城王澄宣旨，敕臣等議都洛。

translations.literal: Pi said, "Your Majesty last year personally led the Six Armies to punish the Xiao clan and reached Luoyang; Prince of Renyang Cheng proclaimed the intent and ordered your servants to debate moving the capital to Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Pi said, "Last year Your Majesty led the Six Armies against the Xiao house to Luoyang; Prince of Renyang Cheng ordered us to debate moving the capital to Luo.

sentences.zh: 初奉恩旨，心情惶越。

translations.literal: When I first received the gracious command my heart was anxious and unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: When I first received the command my heart was anxious.

sentences.zh: 凡欲遷移，當訊之卜筮，審定吉否，然後可。

translations.literal: Whenever one wishes to migrate one should consult divination by milfoil and tortoise and determine fortune or ill fortune—only then may one act."
translations.idiomatic: Any migration should ask the milfoil and tortoise and fix fortune or ill fortune—only then act."

sentences.zh: 」高祖謂丕曰：「往在鄴中，司徒公誕、咸陽王禧、尚書李沖等皆欲請龜占移洛吉凶之事。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said to Pi, "Formerly at Ye, Duke of Works Dan, Prince of Xianyang Xi, and Director of the Masters of Writing Li Chong all wished to request tortoise divination for the fortune of moving to Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said to Pi, "At Ye, Dan Duke of Works, Xi Prince of Xianyang, and Li Chong all wished to divine moving to Luo.

sentences.zh: 朕時謂誕等曰，昔周邵卜宅伊洛，乃識至兆。

translations.literal: I then told Dan and the others that in antiquity the Duke of Zhou divined the site at Yiluo and so knew the utmost omen.
translations.idiomatic: I told them that in antiquity the Duke of Zhou divined Yiluo and knew the utmost omen.

sentences.zh: 今無若斯之人，卜亦無益。

translations.literal: Now there is no one like him; divination is also of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Now there is no one like him; divination is useless.

sentences.zh: 然卜者所以決疑，此既不疑，何須卜也。

translations.literal: Yet divination exists to resolve doubt; here there is no doubt—why need divination?
translations.idiomatic: Divination resolves doubt; here there is no doubt—why divine?

sentences.zh: 昔軒轅卜兆龜焦，卜者請訪諸賢哲，軒轅乃問天老，天老謂為善。

translations.literal: Formerly when Xuanyuan divined, the tortoise scorched; the diviner asked to consult the worthy; Xuanyuan then asked Tian Lao, and Tian Lao said it was good.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanyuan divined, the tortoise scorched; the diviner asked the wise; Xuanyuan asked Tian Lao, who said it was good.

sentences.zh: 遂從其言，終致昌吉。

translations.literal: He followed that word and in the end attained prosperity and good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: He followed that and attained prosperity.

sentences.zh: 然則至人之量未然，審於龜矣。

translations.literal: Thus the utmost man's measure is not yet settled, but is clearer than the tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: The utmost man's measure is not yet settled, yet clearer than tortoise shells.

sentences.zh: 朕既以四海為家，或南或北，遲速無常。

translations.literal: I have already taken the four seas as home; south or north, slow or fast—there is no fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: I have made the four seas my home; south or north, slow or fast—no fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 南移之民，朕自多積倉儲，不令窘乏。

translations.literal: For the people who move south I myself will pile storehouses high so they will not suffer want."
translations.idiomatic: For those who move south I will pile storehouses so they do not suffer want."

sentences.zh: 」丕曰：「臣仰奉慈詔，不勝喜舞。

translations.literal: Pi said, "Your servant respectfully received the gracious command and cannot contain joy and dance."
translations.idiomatic: Pi said, "I received the gracious command and cannot contain my joy."

sentences.zh: 」高祖詔羣官曰：「卿等或以朕無為移徙也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered the officials, "Some of you perhaps think I have no intent to move.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told the officials, "Some of you think I will not move.

sentences.zh: 昔平文皇帝棄背率土，昭成營居盛樂；

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Pingwen abandoned his back to the realm; Emperor Zhaocheng built his dwelling at Shengle;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Pingwen turned his back on the realm; Emperor Zhaocheng built at Shengle;

sentences.zh: 太祖道武皇帝神武應天，遷居平城。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu Daowu by divine martiality answered Heaven and moved his dwelling to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu Daowu by divine martiality answered Heaven and moved to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 朕雖虛寡，幸屬勝殘之運，故移宅中原，肇成皇宇。

translations.literal: I, though empty and few, have the good fortune to belong to an age that conquers the cruel; therefore I move my house to the central plain and begin the imperial realm.
translations.idiomatic: I, though empty and few, have fortune in an age that conquers the cruel; therefore I move to the central plain and begin the imperial realm.

sentences.zh: 卿等當奉先君令德，光迹洪規。

translations.literal: You all should uphold the former lords' excellent virtue and glorify their great model.
translations.idiomatic: You should carry forward our forebears' virtue and magnify their grand example.

sentences.zh: 」前懷州刺史青龍，前秦州刺史呂受恩等仍守愚固，帝皆撫而答之，辭屈而退。

translations.literal: " The former Huaizhou governor Qinglong, former Qinzhou governor Lü Shouen, and others still clung stubbornly to their views; the emperor soothed them all in reply, and they withdrew after being defeated in argument.
translations.idiomatic: " Former governors Qinglong of Huaizhou and Lü Shouen of Qinzhou still held obstinately to the old view; the emperor answered each with reassurance until they were silenced and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝又將北巡，丕遷太傅、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The emperor was again about to tour the north; Pi was moved to Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor prepared another northern tour, Pi was appointed Grand Tutor and put in charge of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 頻表固讓，詔斷表啟，就家拜授。

translations.literal: He memorialized repeatedly to decline firmly; an edict cut off further memorials and granted the appointment at his home.
translations.idiomatic: Pi memorialized again and again to refuse; the court forbade further petitions and invested him at his residence.

sentences.zh: 及車駕發代，丕留守，詔曰：「中原始構，須朕營視，在代之事，一委太傅。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage set out from Dai, Pi remained as guardian. The edict said: "The Central Plains are newly founded and need my personal oversight; affairs in Dai are entirely entrusted to the Grand Tutor."
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor left Dai, Pi stayed behind. The edict ran: "The heartland is still being built and requires my attention; everything in Dai is left to the Grand Tutor."

sentences.zh: 」賜上所乘車馬，往來府省。

translations.literal: He was given the emperor's own carriage and horses for going to and from the government offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the ruler's own carriage and horses for travel to and from the ministries.

sentences.zh: 丕雅愛本風，不達新式，至於變俗遷洛，改官制服，禁絕舊言，皆所不願。

translations.literal: Pi dearly loved the old ways and did not grasp the new style; changing customs and moving the capital to Luoyang, reforming offices and dress, and banning the old speech—all were unwelcome to him.
translations.idiomatic: Pi clung to the northern ways and resisted the new order: sinicizing custom, moving the capital to Luoyang, changing offices and dress, and forbidding the old tongue—all of it displeased him.

sentences.zh: 高祖知其如此，亦不逼之，但誘示大理，令其不生同異。

translations.literal: Gaozu knew this about him and did not press him, only guiding him with great principle so he would not breed dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu understood this and did not force him, only setting out the larger rationale so he would not stir opposition.

sentences.zh: 至於衣冕已行，朱服列位，而丕猶常服列在坐隅。

translations.literal: When court robes were already in use and vermilion dress filled the ranks, Pi still wore ordinary clothes seated at the corner.
translations.idiomatic: Though court robes and scarlet ranks were already in use, Pi still sat in plain dress off to the side.

sentences.zh: 晚乃稍加弁帶，而不能修飾容儀。

translations.literal: Only later did he somewhat add cap and belt, but could not polish his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Only later did he add cap and belt a little, yet he never managed a polished appearance.

sentences.zh: 高祖以丕年衰體重，亦不強責。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because Pi was aged and heavy-bodied, did not strongly demand it.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, seeing Pi's age and bulk, did not insist.

sentences.zh: 及罷降非太祖子孫及異姓王者，雖較於公爵，而利享封邑，亦不快。

translations.literal: When non-Taizu descendants and those of other surnames enfeoffed as kings were demoted, though reduced to dukes they still enjoyed fief revenues—Pi was displeased about this too.
translations.idiomatic: When kings who were not Taizu's descendants or of other surnames were demoted, though cut to ducal rank they still kept fief income—Pi was unhappy even with that.

translations.literal: 〈Doubtful〉
translations.idiomatic: Passage marked doubtful.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 高祖南征，丕表乞少留，思更圖後舉。

translations.literal: When Gaozu campaigned south, Pi memorialized begging to remain a while longer, planning again for a later effort.
translations.idiomatic: During Gaozu's southern campaign Pi asked leave to stay behind awhile, intending to try again later.

sentences.zh: 會司徒馮誕薨，詔六軍反斾。

translations.literal: When Minister over the Masses Feng Dan died, an edict ordered the six armies to turn their banners back.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Feng Dan died, an edict recalled the six armies.

sentences.zh: 丕又以熙薨于代都，表求鑾駕親臨。

translations.literal: Pi also memorialized because Feng Xi had died at the Dai capital, requesting the imperial carriage attend in person.
translations.idiomatic: Pi also memorialized that Feng Xi had died at Dai and begged the emperor to come in person.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「今洛邑肇構，跂望成勞，開闢暨今，豈有以天子之重，遠赴舅國之喪？

translations.literal: The edict said: "Luoyang is newly founded; eager hope and toil await completion. From the founding until now, how could one with the weight of the Son of Heaven travel far for a funeral in the maternal-kin state?"
translations.idiomatic: The reply said: "Luoyang is only now rising; the realm waits on that labor. Since the founding, when has a Son of Heaven gone far away for a maternal uncle's mourning?"

sentences.zh: 朕縱欲為孝，其如大孝何？

translations.literal: Even if I wished to act as a filial son, what of the greater filial duty?
translations.idiomatic: Even if I wished private filial piety, what of the greater filial duty to the realm?

sentences.zh: 縱欲為義，其如大義何？

translations.literal: Even if I wished to act with righteousness, what of the greater righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: Even if I wished private righteousness, what of the greater righteousness owed the state?

sentences.zh: 天下至重，君臣道懸，豈宜苟相誘引，陷君不德。

translations.literal: The realm is paramount; the bond between ruler and minister is weighty—how can you lightly entice and lead the sovereign into unworthy conduct?
translations.idiomatic: The empire outweighs all else; ruler and minister stand far apart—how can you coax the throne into discreditable conduct?

sentences.zh: 令、僕已下可付法官貶之。

translations.literal: The Director and Vice Director and those below may be handed to the judicial officers for demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The Director, Vice Director, and their subordinates are to be referred to the judges for censure.

sentences.zh: 」又詔以丕為都督，領并州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict also appointed Pi commander-in-chief and governor of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made area commander and given Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 後詔以平陽畿甸，改封新興公。

translations.literal: Later an edict, because Pingyang lay in the capital district, changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because Pingyang lay in the metropolitan belt, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 初，李沖又德望所屬，既當時貴要，有杖情，[15]遂與子超娶沖兄女，即伯尚妹也。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Chong was one to whom moral standing was attributed; he was then an eminent figure of the time. Pi had a private leaning [15], and his son Chao married Chong's elder brother's daughter—that is, Bo Shang's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong had long stood for integrity and was then among the great men at court. Pi leaned on that tie [15] and had his son Chao marry Chong's niece, the sister of Bo Shang.

sentences.zh: 丕前妻子隆同產數人，皆與別居。

translations.literal: Pi's sons by his first wife, Long and several full brothers, all lived apart.
translations.idiomatic: Long and the other sons of Pi's first wife each kept separate households.

sentences.zh: 後得宮人，所生同宅共產。

translations.literal: Later he obtained palace women; those born to them shared one house and property.
translations.idiomatic: Later palace women bore him children who lived together under one roof and shared the estate.

sentences.zh: 父子情因此偏。

translations.literal: Father-son affection was thus skewed.
translations.idiomatic: Affection between father and sons was thereby skewed.

sentences.zh: 丕父子大意不樂遷洛。

translations.literal: Pi and his sons were broadly displeased with the move to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pi and his sons were deeply unhappy about the transfer to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖之發平城，太子恂留於舊京，及將還洛，隆與超等密謀留恂，因舉兵斷關，規據陘北。

translations.literal: When Gaozu set out from Pingcheng, Crown Prince Xun remained in the old capital; as he was about to return to Luoyang, Long and Chao secretly plotted to keep Xun behind, raise troops to block the passes, and seize the country north of Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu left Pingcheng, Crown Prince Xun stayed in the old capital; on the return to Luoyang, Long and Chao plotted to detain Xun, cut the passes by force, and hold the region north of Xiao.

sentences.zh: 時丕以老居并州，雖不預其始計，而隆、超咸以告丕。

translations.literal: Pi was then old and living in Bingzhou; though he had not joined the initial plan, Long and Chao both told him.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was aged and in Bingzhou and had not joined the first design, but Long and Chao both informed him.

sentences.zh: 丕外慮不成，口雖致難，心頗然之。

translations.literal: Outwardly fearing failure, though his mouth spoke objections, in his heart he rather approved.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he doubted success and spoke against it, yet inwardly he inclined to agree.

sentences.zh: 及高祖幸平城，推穆泰等首謀，隆兄弟並是黨。

translations.literal: When Gaozu came to Pingcheng and traced Mu Tai and others as chief plotters, the Long brothers were all accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu reached Pingcheng and fixed on Mu Tai and the rest as ringleaders, the Long brothers were counted among the party.

sentences.zh: 丕亦隨駕至平城，每於測問，令丕坐觀。

translations.literal: Pi also followed the imperial progress to Pingcheng; at each interrogation he was made to sit and watch.
translations.idiomatic: Pi followed the court to Pingcheng and was made to sit by while each interrogation proceeded.

sentences.zh: 隆、超與元業等兄弟並以謀逆伏誅。

translations.literal: Long, Chao, and the Yuan Ye brothers and the rest were all executed for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Long, Chao, and the Yuan Ye brothers were all put to death for treason.

sentences.zh: 有司奏處孥戮，詔以丕應連坐，但以先許不死之詔，躬非染逆之身，聽免死，仍為太原百姓，其後妻二子聽隨。

translations.literal: The officials memorialized that their families be exterminated to the third degree; an edict held that Pi should share guilt, but because of an earlier promise that he would not die and because he had not personally joined the rebellion, he was spared death and reduced to a commoner of Taiyuan; his later wife and two sons were allowed to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: The court proposed exterminating their kin; an edict held Pi liable yet, citing the earlier pledge of life and his lack of direct guilt, spared him for commoner status in Taiyuan, letting his later wife and two sons accompany him.

sentences.zh: 隆、超母弟及餘庶兄弟，皆徙敦煌。

translations.literal: Long and Chao's mother-born younger brothers and the remaining lesser brothers were all banished to Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The uterine brothers of Long and Chao and the other collateral kin were exiled to Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 丕時年垂八十，猶自平城力載，隨駕至洛陽。

translations.literal: Pi was then nearly eighty, yet still loaded his own baggage at Pingcheng and followed the imperial progress to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Though nearly eighty, Pi still carried his own baggage from Pingcheng and followed the court to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖每遣左右慰勉之，乃還晉陽。

translations.literal: Gaozu repeatedly sent attendants to comfort and encourage him; only then did he return to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent attendants again and again to console him before he went back to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，丕自并州來赴，世宗引見之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Pi came from Bingzhou to attend the funeral; Emperor Xuanwu received him.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu's death Pi came from Bingzhou to mourn; Xuanwu granted him an audience.

sentences.zh: 以丕舊老，禮有加焉。

translations.literal: Because Pi was an elder of the former reign, courtesy toward him was increased.
translations.idiomatic: As a survivor of the old court, he was shown added respect.

sentences.zh: 尋敕留洛陽。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to remain in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to stay in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後宴于華林都亭，特令二子扶侍坐起。

translations.literal: Later, at a banquet in the Hualin Pavilion, he was specially allowed two sons to support him in sitting and rising.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a feast in the Hualin Pavilion, two sons were specially assigned to help him sit and stand.

sentences.zh: 丕仕歷六世，垂七十年，位極公輔，而還為民庶，然猶心戀京邑，不能自絕人事。

translations.literal: Pi had served through six reigns for nearly seventy years, reaching the highest ministerial rank yet ending as a commoner; still he yearned for the capital and could not cut himself off from public life.
translations.idiomatic: He had served six reigns for nearly seventy years, risen to chief minister, then fallen to commoner rank, yet still clung to the capital and could not withdraw from the world.

sentences.zh: 尋詔以丕為三老。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed one of the Three Elders.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named one of the Three Elders.

sentences.zh: 景明四年薨，年八十二。

translations.literal: In Jingming year 4 he died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jingming year 4 at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 詔贈左光祿大夫、冀州刺史，諡曰平。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously appointed him Left Grand Master of Splendid Service and regional inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Ping.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Left Grand Master of Splendid Service and inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous name Ping.

sentences.zh: 長子隆，先以反誅。

translations.literal: His eldest son Long had earlier been executed for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Long had already been executed for rebellion.

sentences.zh: 隆弟乙升、超，亦同誅。

translations.literal: Long's younger brothers Yisheng and Chao were executed together.
translations.idiomatic: Long's brothers Yisheng and Chao were executed with him.

sentences.zh: 超弟儁、邕，並有軍功。

translations.literal: Chao's younger brothers Jun and Yong both had military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's younger brothers Jun and Yong both won distinction in war.

sentences.zh: 儁封新安縣男，邕封涇縣男。

translations.literal: Jun was enfeoffed Baron of Xin'an; Yong was enfeoffed Baron of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was made Baron of Xin'an; Yong, Baron of Jing.

sentences.zh: 淮陵侯大頭，烈帝之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Marquis Datou of Huailing was a great-grandson of Emperor Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Datou, Marquis of Huailing, was a great-grandson of Emperor Lie.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，擢為內三郎。

translations.literal: Skilled in mounted archery, he was promoted to Inner Third-Rank Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in mounted archery, he rose to Inner Third-Rank Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 從世祖有戰功，賜爵。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Taiwu he had battle merit and was granted a noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taiwu in campaigns, earned merit, and received a noble title.

sentences.zh: 高宗初，封淮陵。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Wencheng's reign he was enfeoffed Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: At Wencheng's accession he was enfeoffed at Huailing.

sentences.zh: 性謹密，帝甚重之。

translations.literal: By nature cautious and reserved, the emperor valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and discreet by nature, he was greatly esteemed at court.

sentences.zh: 位寧北將軍，遷右將軍。

translations.literal: He reached General Who Pacifies the North and was moved to Right General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Pacifies the North, then Right General.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈高平公，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Duke of Gaoping, with the posthumous title Lie.
translations.idiomatic: At death he was posthumously made Duke of Gaoping with the posthumous name Lie.

sentences.zh: 河間公齊，烈帝之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Duke Qi of Hejian was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, Duke of Hejian, was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Lie.

sentences.zh: 少雄傑魁岸，世祖愛其勇壯，引侍左右。

translations.literal: In youth he was heroic and imposing; Emperor Taiwu loved his courage and kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was towering and bold; Taiwu admired his valor and kept him close.

sentences.zh: 從征赫連昌，世祖馬蹶，賊眾逼帝，齊以身蔽捍，決死擊賊，賊乃退，世祖得上馬。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Helian Chang the emperor's horse stumbled and the enemy pressed the emperor; Qi shielded him with his body, fought the enemy to the death, and the enemy withdrew so the emperor could remount.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Helian Chang the emperor's mount stumbled and the foe closed in; Qi covered him bodily, fought as if to die, drove the enemy back, and the emperor remounted.

sentences.zh: 是日微齊，世祖幾至危殆。

translations.literal: That day, but for Qi, the emperor would nearly have reached mortal peril.
translations.idiomatic: That day, without Qi, the emperor would almost have perished.

sentences.zh: 世祖以微服入其城，齊固諫，不許，乃與數人從世祖入。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered the city in plain dress, Qi firmly remonstrated but was not heeded; he then followed the emperor in with several men.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered the city in disguise, Qi protested in vain and followed in with a few men.

sentences.zh: 城內既覺，諸門悉閉。

translations.literal: Once inside the city was alerted and every gate was shut.
translations.idiomatic: The city soon discovered them and every gate was shut.

sentences.zh: 世祖及齊等因入其宮中，得婦人裙，繫之槊上，世祖乘而上，因此得拔，齊有力焉。

translations.literal: The emperor and Qi and the others then entered the palace, obtained a woman's skirt, tied it to a spear, and the emperor climbed it and thus escaped—Qi had strength in this.
translations.idiomatic: They entered the palace, took a woman's skirt, lashed it to a spear, and the emperor climbed out on it—Qi had the strength for that escape.

sentences.zh: 賜爵浮陽侯。

translations.literal: He was granted the marquisate of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Marquis of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 從征和龍，以功拜尚書，進爵為公。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Helong he was appointed Master of Writing for merit and advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: On the Helong campaign he was made Master of Writing for merit and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 後與新興王俊討禿髮保周，坐事免官爵。

translations.literal: Later, with the Prince of Xinxing Jun he attacked Tufa Baozhou and was stripped of office and rank for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning with Prince Jun of Xinxing against Tufa Baozhou, he lost office and rank for an offense.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆將裴方明陷仇池，世祖復授齊前將軍，與建興公古弼討之，遂克仇池，威振羌氐。

translations.literal: When Liu Yilong's general Pei Fangming took Chouchi, the emperor again appointed Qi Forward General and, with Duke of Jianxing Gu Bibie, attacked him; they took Chouchi and awed the Qiang and Di.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yilong's general Pei Fangming seized Chouchi, Taiwu again made Qi Forward General; with Gu Bibie, Duke of Jianxing, he recovered Chouchi and overawed the Qiang and Di.

sentences.zh: 復賜爵河間公，與武都王楊保宗對鎮駱谷。

translations.literal: He was again granted the dukedom of Hejian and, with Prince Baozong of Wudu Yang, jointly garrisoned Luogu.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Duke of Hejian and, with Yang Baozong, Prince of Wudu, jointly held Luogu.

sentences.zh: 時保宗弟文德說保宗閉險自固。

translations.literal: At the time Baozong's younger brother Wende urged Baozong to shut the passes and hold himself fast.
translations.idiomatic: Then Baozong's brother Wende urged him to close the defiles and stand on his own.

sentences.zh: 有期矣，秦州主簿邊因知之，密告齊。

translations.literal: The time was set; Qinzhou registrar Bian Yin learned of it and secretly informed Qi.
translations.idiomatic: A date was fixed; Bian Yin, registrar of Qinzhou, learned of it and secretly told Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊晨詣保宗，呼曰：「古弼至，欲宣詔。

translations.literal: At dawn Qi went to Baozong and called out: "Gu Bibie has arrived and wishes to proclaim the edict."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Qi went to Baozong and shouted: "Gu Bibie is here to proclaim the edict."

sentences.zh: 」保宗出，齊叱左右扶保宗上馬，馳驛送臺。

translations.literal: Baozong came out; Qi ordered his attendants to seize Baozong, put him on a horse, and rush him by post to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Baozong came out; Qi had his men seize him, mount him, and post him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 諸氐遂推文德為主，求援於劉義隆。

translations.literal: The Di then made Wende their leader and sought aid from Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: The Di thereupon set up Wende and asked Liu Yilong for help.

sentences.zh: 義隆遣將房亮之、苻昭、啖龍等率眾助文德。

translations.literal: Yilong sent the generals Fang Liangzhi, Fu Zhao, and Tan Long with troops to aid Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong sent Fang Liangzhi, Fu Zhao, Tan Long, and others to support Wende.

sentences.zh: 齊擊斬殺龍，擒亮之。

translations.literal: Qi struck, killed Long, and captured Liangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi attacked, killed Tan Long, and captured Fang Liangzhi.

sentences.zh: 氐遂平。

translations.literal: The Di were then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Di were pacified.

sentences.zh: 以功拜內都大官。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Grand Inner Steward.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit he was made Grand Inner Steward.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: On his death his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At death his posthumous name was Jing.

sentences.zh: 長子陵，襲爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ling inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ling succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 陵性抗直，天安初，為乙渾所害。

translations.literal: Ling was upright and unyielding; in the first year of Tian'an he was killed by Yihun.
translations.idiomatic: Ling was blunt and unyielding; in Tian'an year 1 Yihun killed him.

sentences.zh: 陵弟蘭，以忠謹見寵。

translations.literal: Ling's younger brother Lan was favored for loyalty and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's brother Lan won favor for loyalty and care.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，賜爵建陽子。

translations.literal: At the start of Gaozu's reign he was granted the viscountcy of Jianyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozu's accession he was made Viscount of Jianyang.

sentences.zh: 卒於武川鎮將。

translations.literal: He died as garrison commander of Wuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died while commanding Wuchuan garrison.

sentences.zh: 子志，字猛略。

translations.literal: His son Zhi, courtesy name Menglue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi, styled Menglue.

sentences.zh: 少清辯強幹，歷覽書傳，頗有文才。

translations.literal: In youth he was clear in debate and strong in execution; he read widely in books and records and had considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was sharp in debate and forceful in action, widely read, and gifted in letters.

sentences.zh: 為洛陽令，不避強禦，與御史中尉李彪爭路，俱入見，面陳得失。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Luoyang he did not avoid the powerful; he disputed the road with Censor-in-Chief Li Biao, and both entered audience to state their case face to face.
translations.idiomatic: As Luoyang magistrate he did not yield to the mighty; he quarreled over the road with Censor-in-Chief Li Biao, and both went in to argue their case before the throne.

sentences.zh: 彪言，御史中尉避承華車蓋，駐論道劍鼓，安有洛陽縣令與臣抗衡。

translations.literal: Biao said: "The censor-in-chief yields to the Chengua carriage canopy, halts for the Way of the sword and drum—how can a Luoyang magistrate contend with a minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Biao said: "The censor-in-chief yields to the Chengua canopy and halts for the imperial sword-and-drum procession—how can a county magistrate stand against a minister?"

sentences.zh: 志言神鄉縣主，普天之下誰不編戶，豈有俯同眾官，避中尉？

translations.literal: Zhi said: "I am magistrate of the divine capital; under heaven who is not a registered household—how can I bow like the common officials and yield to the censor-in-chief?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied: "I govern the sacred capital; who under heaven is not a registered subject—why should I bow like other officials to the censor-in-chief?"

sentences.zh: [16]高祖曰：「洛陽我之豐沛，自應分路揚鑣。

translations.literal: [16] Gaozu said: "Luoyang is my Feng and Pei; naturally we should part ways."
translations.idiomatic: [16] Gaozu said: "Luoyang is my Feng and Pei; of course our roads should diverge."

sentences.zh: 自今以後，可分路而行。

translations.literal: From now on you may each take a separate road."
translations.idiomatic: "Henceforth you may each keep to your own side of the road."

sentences.zh: 」及出，與彪折尺量道，各取其半。

translations.literal: On leaving, he and Biao measured the road with a folding rule and each took half.
translations.idiomatic: Outside, he and Biao measured the street with a folding rule and each took half.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂邢巒曰：「此兒竟可，所謂王孫公子，不鏤自雕。

translations.literal: Gaozu said to Xing Luan: "This boy is truly capable—what they call a lord's son who needs no carving to shine."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told Xing Luan: "The lad has spirit—a true prince's son who needs no chasing to gleam."

sentences.zh: 」巒曰：「露枝霜條，故多勁節，非鸞則鳳，其在本枝也。

translations.literal: Luan said: "Frosted branches and dewy twigs have many strong joints; if not a phoenix then a simurgh—they belong on the main bough."
translations.idiomatic: Luan said: "Frosted boughs bear stout joints; phoenix or simurgh, they belong on the parent stem."

sentences.zh: 」員外郎馮俊，昭儀之弟，恃勢恣撾所部里正。

translations.literal: Staff member Feng Jun, younger brother of Lady Zhaoyi, relied on his backing to beat the village headmen under him at will.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jun, an outer-office attendant and brother of Lady Zhaoyi, bullied the village heads in his district at will.

sentences.zh: 志令主吏收繫，處刑除官。

translations.literal: Zhi ordered the chief clerk to arrest and bind him, punished him, and removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had the chief clerk seize him, punished him, and struck him from office.

sentences.zh: 由此忤旨，左遷太尉主簿。

translations.literal: For this he offended the throne and was demoted to secretary of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: This offended the throne and he was demoted to secretary under the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 俄為從事中郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 車駕南征，高祖微服觀戰所，有箭欲犯帝，志以身障之，高祖便得免。

translations.literal: On the southern campaign the emperor went in disguise to observe the battlefield; an arrow was about to strike the emperor and Zhi shielded him with his body, so the emperor escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign Gaozu went in disguise to watch the fighting; as an arrow was about to strike him, Zhi covered him with his body and the emperor was spared.

sentences.zh: 矢中志目，因此一目喪明。

translations.literal: The arrow struck Zhi in the eye, and he lost sight in that eye.
translations.idiomatic: The shaft struck Zhi's eye, and he lost sight in it.

sentences.zh: 以志行恒州事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhi to administer Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to govern Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，除荊州刺史，還朝，御史中尉王顯奏志在州日，抑買良人為婢，兼剩請供。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanwu's time he was appointed regional inspector of Jingzhou; on returning to court, Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian memorialized that while in the province Zhi had coerced purchase of free persons as slave-girls and also overclaimed supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuanwu he became inspector of Jingzhou; back at court, Censor Wang Xian charged that in the province he had forced free people into bondage as maidservants and skimmed supplies.

sentences.zh: 會赦免。

translations.literal: He was pardoned when an amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty cleared him.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，兼廷尉卿。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Xiaozong's reign he concurrently served as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaozong's accession he also served as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 後除揚州刺史，賜爵建忠伯。

translations.literal: Later he was made regional inspector of Yangzhou and granted the barony of Jianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made inspector of Yangzhou and enfeoffed Baron of Jianzhong.

sentences.zh: 志在州威名雖減李崇，亦為荊楚所憚。

translations.literal: In the province his prestige, though less than Li Chong's, still made Jing and Chu fear him.
translations.idiomatic: In office his name, though below Li Chong's, still awed Jing and Chu.

sentences.zh: 尋為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made regional inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 晚年躭好聲伎，在揚州日，侍側將百人，器服珍麗，冠於一時。

translations.literal: In his later years he indulged in music and performers; while in Yangzhou he kept nearly a hundred attendants at his side, with vessels and dress of rare splendor unsurpassed in the age.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he doted on music and players; at Yangzhou nearly a hundred attendants stood by him, with gear and dress unrivaled in splendor.

sentences.zh: 及在雍州，逾尚華侈，聚斂無極，聲名遂損。

translations.literal: In Yongzhou he went further in luxury, amassing wealth without limit, and his reputation suffered.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongzhou he grew still more extravagant, extorted without end, and his repute collapsed.

sentences.zh: 及莫折念生反，詔志為西征都督討之。

translations.literal: When Moqi Niansheng rebelled, an edict made Zhi Western Campaign commander-in-chief to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Moqi Niansheng rose, Zhi was ordered west as campaign commander to crush him.

sentences.zh: 念生遣其弟天生屯隴口，[17]與志相持。

translations.literal: Niansheng sent his younger brother Tiansheng to garrison Longkou [17] and confront Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Niansheng sent his brother Tiansheng to hold Longkou [17] and face Zhi.

sentences.zh: 為賊所乘，遂棄大眾奔還岐州。

translations.literal: Seized by the enemy's advantage, he abandoned the main force and fled back to Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Outmaneuvered, he abandoned the main army and fled to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 賊遂攻城。

translations.literal: The rebels then besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then laid siege.

sentences.zh: 刺史裴芬之疑城人與賊潛通，將盡出之，志不聽。

translations.literal: Regional inspector Pei Fenzhi suspected the townspeople of secret collusion with the rebels and was about to drive them all out; Zhi would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Pei Fenzhi suspected the citizens of colluding with the enemy and meant to expel them all; Zhi refused.

sentences.zh: 城人果開門引賊，鎖志及芬之送念生，見害。

translations.literal: The townspeople indeed opened the gates and admitted the rebels; they chained Zhi and Fenzhi and sent them to Niansheng, who killed them.
translations.idiomatic: The people opened the gates to the rebels, chained Zhi and Fenzhi, sent them to Niansheng, and they were killed.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝初，贈尚書僕射、太保。

translations.literal: At the start of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 扶風公處真，烈帝之後也。

translations.literal: Duke Chuzhen of Fufeng was a descendant of Emperor Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhen, Duke of Fufeng, was descended from Emperor Lie.

sentences.zh: 少以壯烈聞。

translations.literal: In youth he was known for fierce valor.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was famed for boldness.

sentences.zh: 位殿中尚書，賜爵扶風公，委以大政，甚見尊禮。

translations.literal: He reached Director of the Palace Secretariat, was granted the dukedom of Fufeng, was entrusted with great affairs of state, and was greatly honored.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Palace Secretariat, was made Duke of Fufeng, entrusted with major policy, and treated with high honor.

sentences.zh: 吐京胡曹僕渾等叛，招引朔方胡為援。

translations.literal: The Tujing Hu led by Cao Puhun and others rebelled and called in the Shuofang Hu as allies.
translations.idiomatic: The Tujing Hu under Cao Puhun rebelled and summoned Shuofang Hu allies.

sentences.zh: 處真與高涼王那等討滅之。

translations.literal: Chuzhen, with Prince Na of Gaoliang and others, attacked and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhen, with Prince Na of Gaoliang and others, crushed them.

sentences.zh: 性貪婪，在軍烈暴，坐事伏法。

translations.literal: By nature greedy, in the army he was fierce and cruel; for an offense he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy by nature and brutal in the field, he was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 文安公泥，國之疏族也。

translations.literal: Duke Ni of Wen'an was a distant member of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Ni, Duke of Wen'an, was a collateral of the house.

sentences.zh: 性忠直壯烈，有智畫。

translations.literal: By nature loyal, upright, and fierce, with strategic talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was loyal, blunt, and bold, and skilled in planning.

sentences.zh: 太祖厚遇之，賜爵文安公，拜安東將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Daowu treated him generously, granted him the dukedom of Wen'an, and appointed him General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu favored him, made him Duke of Wen'an, and appointed him General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子屈，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Qu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 太宗時居門下，出納詔命。

translations.literal: In Emperor Mingyuan's time he served at the Gate Department, issuing and receiving edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingyuan he served at the Gate Department, handling edicts in and out.

sentences.zh: 性明敏，善奏事，每合上旨，賜爵元城侯，加功勞將軍，與南平公長孫嵩、白馬侯崔玄伯等並決獄訟。

translations.literal: By nature clever and quick, skilled at memorializing, he always matched the sovereign's intent; he was granted the marquisate of Yuancheng, made General of Meritorious Service, and with Duke of Nanping Changgun Song, Marquis of Baima Cui Xuanbo, and others jointly decided lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and quick in memorials, he always hit the mark; he was made Marquis of Yuancheng and General of Meritorious Service, and with Changgun Song of Nanping, Cui Xuanbo of Baima, and others judged legal cases.

sentences.zh: 太宗東巡，命屈行右丞相，山陽侯奚斤行左丞相，命掌軍國，甚有聲譽。

translations.literal: When Mingyuan toured the east he ordered Qu to act as Right Chancellor and Marquis of Shanyang Xi Jin as Left Chancellor, entrusting them with army and state—his reputation was great.
translations.idiomatic: On Mingyuan's eastern tour Qu served as Right Chancellor and Xi Jin of Shanyang as Left, in charge of army and state, and won great repute.

sentences.zh: 後吐京胡與離石胡出以兵等叛，[18]置立將校，外引赫連屈丐。

translations.literal: Later the Tujing Hu and the Lishi Hu led by Chu Yibing and others rebelled [18], set up commanders, and called in Helian Qubing from outside.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Tujing and Lishi Hu under Chu Yibing and others rebelled [18], appointed officers, and called in Helian Qubing.

sentences.zh: 屈督會稽公劉潔、永安侯魏勤捍之，勤沒於陳，潔墜馬，胡執送屈丐，唯屈眾猶存。

translations.literal: Qu directed Duke of Kuaiji Liu Ji and Marquis of Yong'an Wei Qin to resist; Qin perished in battle, Ji fell from his horse and was seized by the Hu and sent to Qubing—only Qu's force remained.
translations.idiomatic: Qu led Liu Ji of Kuaiji and Wei Qin of Yong'an to resist; Qin died in the ranks, Ji fell and was taken to Qubing, and only Qu's troops were left.

sentences.zh: 太宗以屈沒失二將，欲斬之。

translations.literal: Mingyuan, because Qu had lost two generals, wished to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan, angry that Qu had lost two generals, meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 時并州刺史元六頭荒淫怠事，乃赦屈令攝州事。

translations.literal: At the time Bingzhou inspector Yuan Liutou was dissolute and negligent in office, so Qu was pardoned and ordered to act as provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou inspector Yuan Liutou was dissolute and slack, so Qu was spared and told to take over the province.

sentences.zh: 屈縱酒，頗廢政事，太宗積其前後失，檻車徵還，斬於市。

translations.literal: Qu gave himself to drink and largely neglected government; Mingyuan, tallying his earlier and later faults, had him brought back in a caged cart and executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Qu drank heavily and neglected rule; Mingyuan, weighing old and new faults, had him caged back to the capital and beheaded in the market.

sentences.zh: 子磨渾，少為太宗所知。

translations.literal: His son Mohun was known to Mingyuan from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mohun had been known to Mingyuan since boyhood.

sentences.zh: 元紹之逆也，太宗潛隱於外，磨渾與叔孫俊詐云太宗所在。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shao's rebellion came, Mingyuan hid outside the palace; Mohun and Shusun Jun falsely declared where Mingyuan was.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuan Shao's revolt Mingyuan hid outside; Mohun and Shusun Jun feigned knowledge of his whereabouts.

sentences.zh: 紹使帳下二人隨磨渾往，規為逆。

translations.literal: Shao sent two men from his tent to follow Mohun, intending treason.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent two tent guards after Mohun to plot treason.

sentences.zh: 磨渾既得出，便縛帳下詣太宗斬之。

translations.literal: Once Mohun was out, he bound the tent guards and took them to Mingyuan, who executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Mohun got out, bound the guards, brought them to Mingyuan, and they were killed.

sentences.zh: 太宗得磨渾，大喜，因為羽翼。

translations.literal: Mingyuan, gaining Mohun, was greatly pleased and took him as a close supporter.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan rejoiced to have Mohun and made him a close ally.

sentences.zh: 以勳賜爵長沙公，拜尚書，出為定州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the dukedom of Changsha, appointed Master of Writing, and sent out as regional inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made Duke of Changsha and Master of Writing, then sent out as inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷十四 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」，百衲本、南本、汲本、局本卷末有宋人校語云：「魏收書神元平文諸帝子孫列傳亡，後人補以北史，又取高氏小史附益之。

translations.literal: Wei shu juan 14: In the tables of contents of the various editions this juan is marked "deficient." The Baipu, Nan, Ji, and Ju editions all have Song-dynasty collation notes at the end of the juan stating: "The Wei shu biographies of the descendants of Emperors Shenyuan and Pingwen are lost; later persons supplemented them from the Beishi, and also added material from the Gaoshi xiaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei shu juan 14: Several editions mark this scroll deficient in their tables of contents. Baipu, Nan, Ji, and Ju copies carry a Song note at the juan's end: the Shenyuan and Pingwen descendants chapters of Wei Shou are missing; later editors patched them from Beishi and padded them with Gaoshi xiaoshi.

sentences.zh: 後卷魏收舊史亡者皆放此。

translations.literal: Later juan in which Wei Shou's original history is lost all follow this practice.
translations.idiomatic: Later volumes with lacunae in Wei Shou's original follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 」殿本考證云：「魏收書亡，後人所補」。

translations.literal: The Dian edition's textual verification says: "Wei Shou's book is lost; later persons supplemented it."
translations.idiomatic: The Dian edition's Kaozheng says: "Wei Shou's text is gone; what follows is later supplementation."

sentences.zh: 今方隔山 冊府卷二七一

translations.literal: Now separated by mountains. Cefu juan 271
translations.idiomatic: Now the mountains lie between. Cefu juan 271

sentences.zh: 〈三二一四頁〉

translations.literal: 〈folio 3214〉
translations.idiomatic: folio 3214

sentences.zh: 「山」下有「河」字。

translations.literal: Below "mountain" is the character "river."
translations.idiomatic: The graph for "river" appears below "mountain."

sentences.zh: 按文義當有此字。

translations.literal: Comment: By the sense this character should be present.
translations.idiomatic: Note: The sense requires that character.

sentences.zh: 遂廣募空車從京出者 諸本及北史卷一五「募」字空格，今據冊府卷六七八

translations.literal: Then widely recruited empty carts going out from the capital. In all editions and Beishi juan 15 the character "recruit" is left blank; now supplemented according to Cefu juan 678
translations.idiomatic: Then widely recruited empty carts leaving the capital. All editions and Beishi juan 15 leave the graph for "recruit" blank; it is supplied from Cefu juan 678

sentences.zh: 〈八一００頁〉

translations.literal: 〈folio 8100〉
translations.idiomatic: folio 8100

sentences.zh: 補。

translations.literal: Supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: The reading is supplied.

sentences.zh: 至於公事不應送御史 北史卷一五「送」上有「為」字，通志卷八０魏宗室傳「送」下有「名」字。

translations.literal: As to public business not being sent to the censor. Beishi juan 15 has the character "wei" before "send"; Tongzhi juan 80, Wei Imperial Clan biography, has the character "ming" after "send."
translations.idiomatic: On whether public business should be sent to the censor: Beishi juan 15 has wei before "send"; Tongzhi juan 80 (Wei imperial clan) has ming after "send."

sentences.zh: 按「為送」不洽文義。

translations.literal: Comment: "Wei send" does not fit the sense.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "Wei send" will not parse.

sentences.zh: 下文稱元順「不肯與名」，又云：「不宜下隸中尉，送名御史。

translations.literal: Below it says Yuan Shun "would not give the names," and again: "It is not fitting to subordinate them to the censor-in-chief; send the names to the censor."
translations.idiomatic: Below, Yuan Shun "would not supply the names," and again: "They should not be subordinated to the censor-in-chief; the names should go to the censor."

sentences.zh: 」當時所爭在於所謂「公事」即臣僚集會之事，是否開具名冊送御史臺，並非尚書省的「公事」都該送御史臺。

translations.literal: The dispute at the time concerned whether so-called "public business"—that is, assemblies of officials—should have name lists sent to the Censorate, not whether all public business of the Masters of Writing should go to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The fight was over whether "public business"—meetings of officials—required name lists to the Censorate, not whether every secretariat matter belonged there.

sentences.zh: 這裏「送」下當脫「名」字。

translations.literal: Here the character "ming" is missing after "send."
translations.idiomatic: Here ming is lost after "send."

sentences.zh: 又尋魏書崔琰傳晉文陽□傅嘏傳皆云既為中丞百僚震悚 錢氏考異卷三八云：「按三國崔琰、傅嘏二傳，並不云為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Again, searching the Wei shu biography of Cui Yan and the Jin Wenyang□ biography of Fu Jia, both say that once censor-in-chief the hundred officials trembled. Qian's Kaoyi juan 38 says: "Comment: In the Three Kingdoms biographies of Cui Yan and Fu Jia, neither says they served as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Again, Wei shu's Cui Yan and the Jin Wenyang□ life of Fu Jia both say that as censor-in-chief the hundred officials trembled. Qian Daxin, Kaoyi juan 38: "Note: Neither Three Kingdoms life makes them censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 『晉文陽』或疑『晉陽秋』之譌。

translations.literal: 'Jin Wenyang' may be suspected as a corruption for 'Jin Yangqiu.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Jin Wenyang' may corrupt 'Jin Yangqiu.'

sentences.zh: 然嘏魏人，非晉人也。

translations.literal: Yet Jia was a Wei man, not a Jin man.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jia was a Wei subject, not a Jin one.

sentences.zh: 」按此魏書當是王沈魏書。

translations.literal: Comment: This Wei shu should be Wang Shen's Wei shu.
translations.idiomatic: Note: The Wei shu meant here is Wang Shen's book.

sentences.zh: 「晉文陽」或是「晉陽秋」之訛，傅嘏雖魏人，和司馬氏關係很深，可能敍及他的事跡。

translations.literal: "Jin Wenyang" may be a corruption for "Jin Yangqiu"; though Fu Jia was a Wei man, his ties to the Sima clan were deep, and his deeds may have been narrated there.
translations.idiomatic: "Jin Wenyang" may stand for "Jin Yangqiu"; though Jia was Wei-born, his closeness to the Sima house may have put him in that work.

sentences.zh: 萇弟珍字金雀襲爵艾陵男 諸本及北史卷十五「雀」訛「省」，今據墓誌集釋元珍墓誌

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Zhen, courtesy name Jinque, inherited the barony of Ailing. In all editions and Beishi juan 15 "que" is written erroneously as "sheng"; now emended according to the epitaph in Muzhi jishi, Yuan Zhen's epitaph
translations.idiomatic: Chang's brother Zhen, styled Jinque, inherited the barony of Ailing. All editions and Beishi juan 15 write que as sheng; the reading follows Yuan Zhen's epitaph in Muzhi jishi

sentences.zh: 〈圖版四四〉

translations.literal: 〈plate 44〉
translations.idiomatic: plate 44

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: Emended.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 又墓誌稱珍「胙土晉陽男」，不云襲艾陵男。

translations.literal: The epitaph also calls Zhen "enfeoffed lord of Jinyang," and does not say he inherited the barony of Ailing.
translations.idiomatic: The epitaph also calls Zhen enfeoffed at Jinyang, not heir to Ailing.

sentences.zh: 據上文珍父平傳，襲爵松滋侯，又以軍功賜艾陵男。

translations.literal: According to the biography of Zhen's father Ping above, he inherited the marquisate of Songzi and was also granted the barony of Ailing for military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Per the life of Zhen's father Ping above, he inherited Songzi and received Ailing for military merit.

sentences.zh: 平死，長子萇襲松滋侯，其艾陵男爵當由珍襲封，故此傳云云。

translations.literal: When Ping died, the eldest son Chang inherited the marquisate of Songzi; the barony of Ailing should have been inherited by Zhen—hence this biography's wording.
translations.idiomatic: When Ping died, Chang took Songzi; Ailing should have passed to Zhen—hence the biography's wording.

sentences.zh: 據萇傳稱太和降爵，賜艾陵伯，當即在此時改封珍為晉陽男，故誌稱「胙土」，不云「襲爵」。

translations.literal: According to Chang's biography, at the Taihe demotion of ranks he was granted the barony of Ailing as earl—probably at that time Zhen was changed to Baron of Jinyang; hence the epitaph's "enfeoffed territory" and not "inherited title."
translations.idiomatic: Chang's life says that at the Taihe demotion he received Ailing as earl—likely when Zhen was shifted to Jinyang baron, so the epitaph says "fief" rather than "inheritance."

sentences.zh: 傳和誌互見，未必傳誤。

translations.literal: Biography and epitaph illuminate each other; the biography need not be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Life and epitaph complement each other; the biography need not be in error.

sentences.zh: 此類封爵、歷官、名字、諡號等史、誌不同的很多，凡不能斷定史誤者，今後不一一出校記。

translations.literal: Such cases in which enfeoffments, offices, names, and posthumous titles differ between history and epitaph are many; where history's error cannot be fixed, collation notes will not be given each time hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Rank, office, name, and posthumous title often diverge between history and epitaph; where the history cannot be proved wrong, notes will not be repeated for every case.

sentences.zh: 幽州前北平府主簿河間邢杲 通鑑卷一五二

translations.literal: Youzhou, former Beiping prefecture registrar, Xing Guo of Hejian. Zizhi tongjian juan 152
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou, former registrar of Beiping prefecture, Xing Guo of Hejian. Zizhi tongjian juan 152

sentences.zh: 〈四七五０頁〉

translations.literal: 〈folio 4750〉
translations.idiomatic: folio 4750

sentences.zh: 「北平」作「平北」。

translations.literal: "Beiping" is written "Pingbei."
translations.idiomatic: Beiping appears as Pingbei.

sentences.zh: 按北平郡魏屬平州，不屬幽州，也不得稱「府」。

translations.literal: Comment: Beiping commandery in Wei belonged to Pingzhou, not Youzhou, and could not be called a "prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Note: Beiping commandery belonged to Pingzhou, not Youzhou, and could not be styled a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 「平北」乃其時幽州刺史某人所帶的軍號，魏制，五品以上將軍開府置屬，有主簿。

translations.literal: "Pingbei" was a military title borne at the time by a certain regional inspector of Youzhou; under Wei regulations, generals of fifth rank and above who opened an office had registrars.
translations.idiomatic: "Pingbei" was the army title of a Youzhou inspector; under Wei rules, fifth-rank generals and above who opened offices had registrars.

sentences.zh: 這裏「北平」當是「平北」倒誤。

translations.literal: Here "Beiping" should be the inverted error for "Pingbei."
translations.idiomatic: Here Beiping is a transposition for Pingbei.

sentences.zh: 會臺申汰簡所授郡縣 諸本及北史卷一五此句作「會臺申休簡授郡縣」。

translations.literal: When the Secretariat reported culling and simplifying the granted commanderies and counties. In all editions and Beishi juan 15 this sentence reads "When the Secretariat reported rest and simplification in granting commanderies and counties."
translations.idiomatic: When the secretariat reported culling the granted commanderies and counties: all editions and Beishi juan 15 read "When the secretariat reported rest and simplification in granting commanderies and counties."

sentences.zh: 諸本下並注「疑」字。

translations.literal: All editions also annotate "doubtful" below.
translations.idiomatic: All editions also mark "doubtful" below.

sentences.zh: 通志卷八０如上摘句。

translations.literal: Tongzhi juan 80 quotes as above.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi juan 80 has the passage as quoted above.

sentences.zh: 按「休簡授郡縣」不可解，「汰簡所授郡縣」即指汰簡以河北流民設置的僑置郡縣，其中就有原擬以邢杲充任太守的新安郡。

translations.literal: Comment: "Rest and simplification in granting commanderies and counties" cannot be parsed; "culling and simplifying the granted commanderies and counties" refers to culling the refugee prefectures and counties set up for Hebei migrants, among which was Xin'an commandery, originally intended for Xing Guo as administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "Rest and simplification in granting commanderies" is nonsense; "culling the granted commanderies and counties" means trimming the refugee prefectures set up for Hebei migrants, including Xin'an, first slated for Guo.

sentences.zh: 沒有簡去的河間郡又給了杲的從子子瑤，因此「杲深耻恨」。
