translations.literal: The uncleared Hejian commandery was then given to Guo's younger clansman Ziyao, hence "Guo was deeply shamed and resentful."
translations.idiomatic: When Hejian was not cut, it went to Guo's cousin Ziyao, hence Guo's deep shame and resentment.

sentences.zh: 觀前後文，通志是對的，今據改。

translations.literal: Viewing the context before and after, Tongzhi is correct; emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The context shows Tongzhi is right; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 位尚書令雍州刺史歷比部侍郎華州刺史 北史卷一五同。

translations.literal: Held the offices Master of Writing, regional inspector of Yongzhou, and in sequence Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and regional inspector of Huazhou. Beishi juan 15 is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Offices held: Master of Writing, inspector of Yongzhou, and in turn Vice Director of Revenue and inspector of Huazhou. Beishi juan 15 agrees.

sentences.zh: 按此傳簡略，疑有脫文。

translations.literal: Comment: This biography is abbreviated; text is probably missing.
translations.idiomatic: Note: The life is abbreviated; text is likely missing.

sentences.zh: 卷六顯祖紀天安元年記「殿中尚書、鎮西大將軍西河公元石」救懸瓠。

translations.literal: Juan 6, Annals of Emperor Xianzu, Tian'an year 1, records "Director of the Palace Secretariat, Grand General Who Guards the West, Duke of Xihe Yuan Shi" rescuing Xuanchi.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 6 (Xianzu) records that in Tian'an year 1 "Director of the Palace Secretariat, Grand General Who Guards the West, Duke of Xihe Yuan Shi" relieved Xuanchi.

sentences.zh: 其事又見於卷五六鄭羲傳、卷六一常珍奇傳，不應於石本傳不載。

translations.literal: The affair also appears in juan 56, biography of Zheng Yi, and juan 61, biography of Chang Zhenqi—it should not be absent from Shi's own biography.
translations.idiomatic: The same affair appears in juan 56 (Zheng Yi) and juan 61 (Chang Zhenqi) and ought not be missing from Shi's life.

sentences.zh: 且如紀所書，石爵為「西河公」。

translations.literal: Moreover, as the annals write it, Shi's noble rank was "Duke of Xihe."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the annals give Shi the rank Duke of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 此傳不云封爵，但稱「司徒」，亦見缺漏。

translations.literal: This biography does not mention enfeoffment but only calls him "Minister over the Masses"—another sign of lacuna.
translations.idiomatic: This life names no enfeoffment but only "Minister over the Masses"—another lacuna.

sentences.zh: 永受復除 諸本「永」作「求」。

translations.literal: Permanently receive exemption from corvée. In all editions "yong" is written "qiu."
translations.idiomatic: "Permanently receive exemption from corvée": every edition writes yong (permanent) as qiu (seek).

sentences.zh: 按這是元宏給予元丕的特權，並非元丕請求，「求」字不可通。

translations.literal: Comment: This was a special privilege granted by Yuan Hong to Yuan Pi, not something Pi requested; the character "qiu" will not parse.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Yuan Hong granted Yuan Pi this privilege; he did not request it, and qiu will not parse.

sentences.zh: 卷四四苟頹傳、卷九三王叡傳並見「永受復除」語，知這裏「求」乃「永」之訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Juan 44, biography of Gou Ti, and juan 93, biography of Wang Rui, both have the phrase "permanently receive exemption from corvée," showing that here "qiu" is a corruption of "yong"; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 44 (Gou Ti) and juan 93 (Wang Rui) both have "permanently receive exemption from corvée," proving qiu corrupts yong; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 尚書于果曰 諸本「果」作「杲」，通鑑卷一三九

translations.literal: Master of Writing Yu Guo said. In all editions "Guo" is written "Gao"; Zizhi tongjian juan 139
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Yu Guo spoke: all editions write Guo as Gao; Zizhi tongjian juan 139

sentences.zh: 〈四三五二頁〉

translations.literal: 〈folio 4352〉
translations.idiomatic: folio 4352

sentences.zh: 作「果」。

translations.literal: has "Guo."
translations.idiomatic: has Guo.

sentences.zh: 按于果附本書卷三一、北史卷二三于栗磾傳。

translations.literal: Comment: Yu Guo is attached in this book juan 31 and Beishi juan 23, biography of Yu Lüpi.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Yu Guo appears in this book juan 31 and Beishi juan 23 (Yu Lüpi).

sentences.zh: 通鑑是，今據改。

translations.literal: The Tongjian is correct; now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjian is right; the text follows it.

sentences.zh: 中原其如是所由擬 此句不可解，必有訛脫，通鑑卷一三九

translations.literal: The Central Plains are as this passage intends. This sentence cannot be parsed; there must be corruption and lacuna. Zizhi tongjian juan 139
translations.idiomatic: "The Central Plains are as this intends": the line will not parse and must be corrupt or lacunose. Zizhi tongjian juan 139

sentences.zh: 〈四三五二頁〉

translations.idiomatic: folio 4352

sentences.zh: 載于果語，無此句，當亦因不可解而刪去，知訛脫已久。

translations.literal: Recorded in Guoyu; that sentence is absent—probably struck as unintelligible, which shows the corruption and lacuna are old.
translations.idiomatic: Guoyu preserves the passage but not this line; it was likely dropped because it could not be parsed, so the damage is longstanding.

sentences.zh: 雖較於公爵而利享封邑亦不快 北本、殿本及北史卷一五「較」作「駮」。

translations.literal: "Although jiao compared with a duke, yet enjoying the benefit of a fief was still not pleasant": in the Northern edition, Palace edition, and Beishi juan 15, "jiao" (compare) is written "bo" (refute).
translations.idiomatic: The clause "though matched against a duke's standing, the profit of a fief still brought no satisfaction" reads "compare" (jiao) as "refute" (bo) in the Northern and Palace editions and in Beishi juan 15.

sentences.zh: 按大意是說雖降封為公，而享受封邑之利，元丕却仍然不快。

translations.literal: Comment: The general sense is that although demoted in rank to duke and still enjoying the profits of a fief, Yuan Pi nevertheless remained discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Note: The point is that even after reduction to duke and retention of fief income, Yuan Pi was still unhappy.

sentences.zh: 但作「較」或「駮」都不易解，當有訛脫。

translations.literal: But whether written "jiao" or "bo," neither is easy to construe; there must be corruption and lacuna.
translations.idiomatic: Neither reading makes good sense; the line is corrupt or incomplete.

sentences.zh: 有杖情 諸本「情」下注「疑」字。

translations.literal: "Having zhang sentiment": in all editions a doubtful mark is entered below "qing" (sentiment).
translations.idiomatic: The phrase "zhang sentiment" carries an editorial "?" after "qing" in every witness.

sentences.zh: 按「杖」同「仗」，「杖情」即依恃之情，無可疑。

translations.literal: Comment: "Zhang" is the same as "zhang" (rely on); "zhang sentiment" means the feeling of reliance—nothing doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "Zhang" equals "rely upon"; "zhang sentiment" means dependence—no emendation is needed.

sentences.zh: 今刪。

translations.literal: Now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: The doubtful mark is removed.

sentences.zh: 豈有俯同眾官避中尉 冊府卷二七一

translations.literal: "How could one bow with the multitude of officials to avoid the Central Commander": Cefu juan 271
translations.idiomatic: "How could one stoop like the other officials to dodge the Central Commander": Cefu juan 271

sentences.zh: 〈三二一四頁〉

translations.idiomatic: folio 3214

sentences.zh: 、通典卷二四御史中尉條「避」上有「趨」字。

translations.literal: , Tongdian juan 24, entry on the Censor Central Commander, has the character "qu" (hasten) above "bi" (avoid).
translations.idiomatic: ; Tongdian juan 24 (Censor Central Commander) inserts "hasten" (qu) before "avoid" (bi).

sentences.zh: 按當時句法，應有此字，當是脫文。

translations.literal: Comment: By the syntax of the period, that character should be present; it is a lacuna.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Contemporary usage requires the word; it dropped from the text.

sentences.zh: 念生遣其弟天生屯隴口 諸本及北史卷一五「隴」作「龍」。

translations.literal: Niansheng sent his younger brother Tiansheng to garrison Longkou: in all editions and Beishi juan 15, "Long" (Long region) is written "Dragon" (long).
translations.idiomatic: Niansheng dispatched his brother Tiansheng to hold Longkou; every edition and Beishi juan 15 write the place name "Long" as "Dragon."

sentences.zh: 通鑑卷一五０

translations.literal: Zizhi tongjian juan 150
translations.idiomatic: See Zizhi tongjian, juan 150

sentences.zh: 〈四六八三頁〉

translations.idiomatic: folio 4683

sentences.zh: 稱元志與天生「戰於隴口」。

translations.literal: states that Yuan Zhi and Tiansheng "fought at Longkou."
translations.idiomatic: has Yuan Zhi and Tiansheng "battle at Longkou."

sentences.zh: 胡注：「隴口，隴坻之口也。

translations.literal: Hu Zhu's note: "Longkou is the mouth of the Long dike."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sanxing glosses Longkou as the pass at the Long plateau.

sentences.zh: 」按卷十肅宗紀正光五年八月，卷五九蕭寶夤傳、卷七三崔延伯傳都說莫折天生在隴東大敗元志。

translations.literal: Comment: Juan 10 Annals of Emperor Suzong, eighth month of Zhenguang year 5; juan 59 Biography of Xiao Baoyin; and juan 73 Biography of Cui Yanbo all say Moqi Tiansheng routed Yuan Zhi east of Long.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Suzong's annals (juan 10, Zhenguang 5.8), Xiao Baoyin's biography (juan 59), and Cui Yanbo's biography (juan 73) all place Moqi Tiansheng's great defeat of Yuan Zhi in Longdong.

sentences.zh: 作「隴」是，今據改。

translations.literal: Writing "Long" is correct; now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: "Long" is the right graph; the text is corrected on that authority.

sentences.zh: 後吐京胡與離石胡出以兵等叛 卷二八劉潔傳「出以兵」作「出以眷」，疑作「眷」是。

translations.literal: Later the Tujing Hu and Lishi Hu, Chuyibing and others, rebelled: juan 28 Biography of Liu Ji writes "Chuyijuan" for "Chuyibing"; "juan" is probably correct.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Tujing and Lishi Hu, with Chuyijuan and others, rose in revolt; Liu Ji's biography (juan 28) reads "Chuyijuan" where this annal has "Chuyibing"—"juan" is likely the true form.
